articles.title: HomePod Mini 2 first look: Three things I love and one disappointment
articles.text:
When I first heard about the new $149 HomePod Mini 2 at Apple’s Welcome Home event last month, I was disappointed. It’s been six years since Apple launched its entry-level smart speaker, and all it got in the second gen was a chip bump, some color glowy stuff, and better AirPlay? For $50 more than the original, which launched at $99, Apple didn’t even upgrade the sound system. It felt like the company phoned this one in.
HomePod Mini 2 first look: Three things I love and one disappointment
The new Mini is faster, quieter, and gorgeous in green, but its upgraded Mac speaker feature didn’t work for me.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
Now that I’ve got my hands on a couple and set them up in my home office, I’m more enthused. The Mini 2 is so much faster than the first-gen Mini, playing music in a few seconds and responding to smart home commands just as quickly. If you’re fed up with standing over your HomePod waiting for it to finally do what you asked, then that alone is worth the upgrade.
Here are my three favorite features of the new Mini 2 after spending a couple days with it, and my one big disappointment.
Siri is much snappier and much less chatty
The biggest upgrade for the Mini 2 is Siri AI, but that isn’t available yet. Apple says it’s coming “later” in a software update. However, the basic smart voice assistant has definitely improved. Siri on the Mini 2 is much snappier than on the first-gen Mini, regularly responding in under three seconds. This is thanks to a newer, faster processor (the S10, up from the S5) and Wi-Fi 6E support (up from Wi-Fi 4).
When I asked Siri to play Taylor Swift, a song started in a couple of seconds. It correctly told me who won this year’s World Series in under two seconds, and turned off the light or opened the shades in under three seconds.
That’s a huge improvement over the up to 10 seconds I often have to wait for Siri to get things done on the first-gen Mini. However, asking something harder, like who will win the US midterm elections, still brings up the familiar offer to look at some web results on my iPhone. As I said, Siri AI isn’t here yet.
The other new behavior I am really enjoying is that when I ask Siri to perform a smart home action, such as open the shades or turn on the lights, instead of “OK, Jen,” or “One sec,” followed by a wordy confirmation of the action that I often get on the first-gen Mini, the Mini 2 just does it and doesn’t talk back. It’s not silent for every action, but it’s quiet enough to be a noticeable improvement.
This Mini is gorgeous in green and sounds great
The green color is divine. This is the prettiest small smart speaker I’ve seen — and I’ve tried them all.
Yes, Amazon’s Echo Dot Max’s purple is fun, the Google Home Speaker’s pale green is elegant, but Apple’s deep green is seriously sophisticated. It’s a color that fits in really well in various places around my home, and I’m so glad the company finally released a green option. It’s a big improvement over the slightly garish yellow and orange of the prior-gen Minis and the best of the new colors.
I saw all the colors in person at Apple’s Welcome Home event, and while the pink is pretty, it’s very pale, and the blue is functionally identical to the first-gen blue, maybe a shade lighter. While a lot of folks will be happy with black (don’t get white unless you plan to dust it regularly), the green is my new go-to.
Two green HomePod Mini 2s look so good on the walnut Nanoleaf monitor stand I’m testing; it’s like my office got an instant upgrade. And while Apple didn’t update the speakers in the Mini 2, it’s still a very good speaker for its size, doing a fine job with Bad Bunny’s bass and delivering clear mids and vocals. While $300 is steep for computer speakers, two as a stereo pair in my office definitely delivered on room-filling sound.
You can finally disable touch
A few weeks ago I fumbled for my phone on my nightstand and accidentally hit the top of my HomePod Mini, blaring music in the bedroom at 3AM. My husband was not happy.
A new setting in the Home app now lets you lock the Mini’s top controls. This goes for all HomePods, old and new, and it’s a major quality-of-life upgrade. How often do you intentionally touch the top of your HomePod? I bet far less often than accidentally!
The other new trick for the top of the HomePod is Sound Glow. This makes the LEDs display colors that match the album art of the song you’re playing (it’s also backward compatible with the first-gen Mini and the second-gen HomePod). It’s neat, but only works with Apple Music and Podcasts and is so subtle that I don’t feel it adds much to my music-listening experience.
Signature feature fail
Beyond the speed improvement, the other new feature I was excited about is the HomePod Mini 2’s ability to be the default speaker for your Mac using what Apple calls “a responsive and persistent AirPlay connection.” This creates a wireless point-to-point connection between the computer and the HomePod.
You can pair a single speaker or a stereo pair to your Mac, and the feature also works with the second-gen HomePod. (Two or four HomePod Mini 2s can also now be part of a surround sound setup using the new Apple TV 4K.)
Disappointingly, I couldn’t get the Mac speaker set up to work. I have the required hardware: a Mac that supports Wi-Fi 6E, running the public release of macOS 27.2 (a Mac Mini M4), and HomePods on HomePod Software 27.2. But the Sound pane in my Mac’s settings didn’t offer an option to set a HomePod via AirPlay as the default sound output.
The Mini showed up and connected like any other AirPlay speaker, with the same flaws as regular AirPlay — occasional artifacting, drop-offs, and some lag with notification sounds — along with the Mac defaulting to its built-in speakers when the computer restarts, or anytime I activate Siri on the HomePod. I also tried with a stereo pair of Minis, but they also played over regular AirPlay.
The chip bump and speed improvements make this a bigger upgrade than it initially seemed
According to a 9to5Mac’s hands-on, when the persistent AirPlay is enabled, the HomePod Mini should show up as a default system output device in the System Information, and there should be an option to enable it under “Play sound effects through” in the Sound pane in System Settings, but neither was there for me. I have seen other reports of the same issue.
I tried resetting both HomePods completely after they updated to 27.2 out of the box (I was on the HomePod Software betas, but 27.2 is now in general release), and the feature still isn’t working. I reached out to Apple, but the company hasn’t responded to my requests yet; I’ll update this article if I hear back or find a solution.
There’s more to come
I’ve only been testing the Mini 2 for two days, and while the real test will come when it gets its Siri AI upgrade, the chip bump and speed improvements make this a bigger upgrade than it initially seemed. Apple does need to work on the Mac pairing feature; it has a lot of potential, but based on my struggles here, it feels unfinished.
I plan to do a full review once Siri AI launches, and of course compare it to Apple’s big new smart home release: the upcoming $299 Apple HomeView smart display. It is also a Home hub, but the screen gives it more functionality. At $149, though, the Mini 2 is now the cheapest way to get an Apple Home hub with Thread and Matter support.

articles.title: ¿A qué hora se estrena 'La edad dorada' temporada 4 en HBO Max?
articles.text:
Año y medio después de su última entrega, por fin llega la temporada 4 de La edad dorada. Este drama de época que ha cautivado al mundo entero regresa con nuevos episodios para volver a conquistar a su público. Creada por Julian Fellowes (Downton Abbey), es una de las producciones más aclamadas y queridas por los fans de los dramas ambientados en el siglo XIX. Pero, ¿a qué hora y dónde se estrena La edad dorada temporada 4?
Bertha Russell cambió la alta sociedad, pero a un alto precio. Ahora, en la temporada 4 de La edad dorada, su familia debe afrontar las consecuencias mientras Agnes van Rhijn aprovecha la oportunidad para recuperar su posición. Mientras tanto, Marian se abre un nuevo camino y Peggy se esfuerza por ganarse la aceptación de sus futuros suegros. En esta nueva era, hay que tener cuidado con lo que se desea.
Acerca de dónde podrá verse, a diferencia de otros títulos, aquí no depende para nada del territorio. En Estados Unidos, España, Latinoamérica y en el resto del mundo, La edad dorada temporada 4 estará disponible en HBO Max. La plataforma alberga los derechos exclusivos de toda la serie, por lo que contará de nuevo con su cuarta entrega en el catálogo. Eso sí, también podrá verse en servicios asociados a HBO Max como Movistar Plus+ o Amazon Prime Video siempre que se pague el extra de suscripción.
Hora de estreno de La edad dorada temporada 4
En cuanto a la hora de estreno de La edad dorada, en Estados Unidos se emitirá el domingo 1 de noviembre a las 9:00 pm E.T. En España y Latinoamérica, llegará a HBO Max en la conversión horaria de cada país:
- España: 2:00 h am del lunes 2 de noviembre.
- México, Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica: 19:00 h.
- Perú, Colombia, Panamá, Ecuador: 20:00 h.
- Chile, Venezuela, Bolivia, República Dominicana, Puerto Rico: 21:00 h.
- Paraguay, Argentina, Brasil, Uruguay: 22:00 h.
Date de alta en HBO MAX y tendrás acceso a las mejores series y películas exclusivas como The Wire, Los Soprano o Casa del Dragón. Incluye todo el catálogo de Warner, los clásicos de Cartoon Network, los grandes estrenos y el mejor deporte.
A partir de ese momento, los fans podrán disfrutar del primer capítulo de la temporada 4 de La edad dorada. A partir de ahí, la serie llevará una estrategia de estreno semanal, con un nuevo episodio todos los domingos por la noche (la madrugada de los lunes en España). Así hasta llegar al octavo y último capítulo, que se estrenará el 20 de diciembre, manteniendo la serie en activo durante más de un mes.

articles.title: Failles PHP : 10 jours après, près de 30 millions de sites et services web toujours vulnérables
articles.text:
Onze jours après la publication des correctifs, la mise à jour de PHP avance… mais le chemin est encore long. Selon le moteur de recherche Censys, 29,6 millions de services PHP exposés sur Internet tournaient encore sur une version vulnérable dans la journée du vendredi 30 octobre 2026. Le moteur, développé par l’entreprise américaine de cybersécurité du même nom, scanne Internet en permanence.
 🚨 Censys is closely tracking PHP2Shell exposure and remediation worldwide.
Our live dashboard tracks affected PHP versions and patching progress by country, network, and PHP version.
View the live dashboard: https://t.co/sicDgpcKz6 https://t.co/wdqjMTZH2m
— Censys (@censysio) October 22, 2026
À lire aussi : « Un échec » cuisant pour la cybersécurité – pourquoi les failles PHP ont plongé une partie d’Internet dans le noir
Une mise à jour qui progresse
Les chiffres de Censys montrent néanmoins que la mise à jour progresse. Quelques jours plus tôt, le 26 octobre, on comptait encore plus de 32 millions de services vulnérables. C’est mieux que le lundi 26 octobre, où l’on en comptait plus de 32 millions. Depuis la mise en ligne des correctifs le 21 octobre, 12,4 millions de services PHP sont passés à une version corrigée du langage de programmation.
La France fait partie des mauvais élèves. Avec un peu plus de 2 millions de services non mis à jour, l’Hexagone se classe au troisième rang mondial des pays les plus vulnérables, derrière les États-Unis (9,1 millions) et l’Allemagne (3,7 millions). Pire, sur dix services PHP français dont la version est connue, huit n’ont toujours pas reçu le correctif. C’est plus que la moyenne mondiale
Notez que ces chiffres doivent être pris avec du recul. Ils reposent en effet sur la version de PHP affichée par les serveurs. Or, 61 % des services ne déclarent pas la version de PHP utilisée. De plus, certaines distributions Linux corrigent la faille sans changer le numéro de version. Il s’agit donc d’une estimation haute, mais qui donne un aperçu de l’état des lieux de la mise à jour.
Les versions de PHP en fin de vie
Sur les 30 millions de services potentiellement vulnérables, environ 24 millions tournent sous PHP 8.1 ou une version plus ancienne. Il s’agit de versions de PHP qui ne sont plus mises à jour par les développeurs de la PHP Foundation. Comme le rappelle le Centre gouvernemental de veille, d’alerte et de réponse aux attaques informatiques (CERT-FR) dans son alerte de sécurité, « l’éditeur n’assure plus le support des versions de PHP 5.x, 7.x, 8.0.x et 8.1.x ». La version la plus répandue sur Internet est d’ailleurs PHP 7.4.33, une version abandonnée… mais toujours présente sur près de 7 millions de services.
Vu la gravité des failles, l’équipe de sécurité de PHP a exceptionnellement publié des correctifs pour PHP 7.4, 8.0 et 8.1, à appliquer soi-même dans le code source. Pour les versions encore plus anciennes, rien n’est prévu à ce stade. Il faut impérativement prévoir une migration vers une version récente de PHP. C’est un processus bien plus lourd qu’une simple mise à jour.
À lire aussi : Failles PHP – pourquoi c’est un vrai casse-tête pour l’Internet mondial
Des cyberattaques en cours
Tandis que les cibles potentielles se mettent à jour, de nombreuses tentatives d’attaques ont été recensées sur Internet. En France, le CERT-FR de l’ANSSI a identifié plusieurs tentatives d’exploitation des failles de PHP. Comme l’expliquent les chercheurs de Tenable, les failles sont difficiles à exploiter à grande échelle. Chaque attaque doit être ajustée à la configuration exacte du serveur visé. Elle peut toutefois toucher en masse des équipements qui partagent le même logiciel.
C’est d’ailleurs ce qu’il s’est produit il y a quelques jours dans le cadre de la première cyberattaque réussie exploitant les failles PHP en conditions réelles. Des pirates chinois sont en effet parvenus à prendre le contrôle total de 25 serveurs aux États-Unis, au Japon, à Taïwan et en Corée du Sud. Les assaillants ont combiné PHP2Shell avec une faille du noyau Linux pour arriver à leurs fins. La CISA, l’agence américaine de cybersécurité, confirme que les deux failles sont activement exploitées dans des cyberattaques.
 👉🏻 Suivez l’actualité tech en temps réel : ajoutez 01net à vos sources sur Google, et abonnez-vous à notre canal WhatsApp.
Source : Censys

articles.title: Trotz KI-Rückstand: Apple-CEO John Ternus äußert sich zufrieden über die aktuelle Position des Unternehmens
articles.text:
„Die Produktentwicklung ist etwas zutiefst Menschliches“: Apple-CEO äußert sich zu KI-Rückstand
In den vergangenen Jahren wurde Apple oft vorgeworfen, bei der KI-Entwicklung den Anschluss zu verpassen. Das galt insbesondere für die verzögerte Veröffentlichung von Siri AI. CEO John Ternus vertritt allerdings eine ganz andere Meinung. Im Interview mit Wired erklärte er: „Mir gefällt unsere derzeitige Position sehr gut.“
Siri AI ist endlich verfügbar – aber nicht in der EU
Ternus ist erst seit zwei Monaten CEO von Apple, im Unternehmen aber kein Neuling. Er begann seine Karriere bei dem iPhone-Hersteller im Jahr 2001 und arbeitete zuletzt als Senior Vice President of Hardware Engineering, bevor er am 1. September 2026 CEO wurde. „John hat von Natur aus ein Gespür für großartige Produkte, und genau das macht Apple aus“, so Greg Joswiak, Apples Senior Vice President für weltweites Marketing, gegenüber Wired. „Das kann man nicht lernen.“ Seit seiner Beförderung hat Ternus zahlreiche Produktneuheiten enthüllt, zuletzt beispielsweise den ersten Mac mit Touchscreen. Besonderen Applaus erntete der CEO, als er bekannt gab, dass das neue Gerät die Beleuchtung des Apple-Logos zurückbringt. In einer Zeit, die von KI geprägt ist, sendet das Unternehmen damit ein wichtiges Signal: Hardware ist nach wie vor entscheidend.
Aber welche Rolle soll KI künftig bei neuen Produkten spielen? Bisher agierte Apple in diesem Bereich eher zurückhaltend. Im Juni 2024 stellte das Unternehmen schließlich Apple Intelligence vor. Das KI-Paket sollte zum Verkaufsschlager für die iPhone-16-Serie werden. Dann folgte allerdings ein Rückschlag: Als die iPhones auf den Markt kamen, war Apple Intelligence noch nicht installiert. Es wurde erst später mit iOS 18.1 nachgeliefert. EU-Nutzer:innen erhielten sogar erst mit iOS 18.4 Zugriff darauf. Auch die Veröffentlichung der KI-Version von Siri wurde mehrfach verschoben. Erst mit iOS 27 erschien Siri AI – das gilt allerdings nicht für die EU. Grund dafür sind die Vorgaben des Digital Markets Act, die Apple bisher nicht erfüllen konnte.
Die Produktentwicklung soll menschlich bleiben
Trotz der Rückschläge könnte Apple jetzt im Vorteil sein. Der erste große KI-Hype ist längst abgeflacht und viele Nutzer:innen sind von übermäßigen KI-Funktionen eher genervt als begeistert. Ein Beispiel ist Windows 11: Microsoft verfolgte mit der Einführung des neuen Betriebssystems eine aggressive KI-Strategie, die nicht bei allen gut ankam. Inzwischen hat das Unternehmen die KI-Funktionen wieder reduziert, um die Nutzungserfahrung zu verbessern. Zuvor hatte Microsoft sogar den Texteditor Notepad mit KI ausgestattet – obwohl dieser gerade wegen seines minimalistischen Designs bei den Nutzer:innen beliebt ist. Diese KI-Überfrachtung hat dazu geführt, dass viele einen Wechsel zu Windows 11 ablehnten. Noch heute laufen laut Statcounter rund ein Viertel der PCs mit dem Vorgängersystem, obwohl der offizielle Support längst eingestellt wurde.
„Wir waren selten die Ersten”, soll der ehemalige Apple-CEO Tim Cook laut Bloomberg im vergangenen Jahr in einem internen Meeting gesagt haben. Das könnte dem Konzern jetzt zugutekommen. Während die Risiken der Technologie derzeit die öffentliche Debatte prägen, sieht Apple laut Ternus keinen Selbstzweck darin. KI solle nur dort zum Einsatz kommen, wo sie einen echten Mehrwert liefern kann. „Wir alle lesen die Berichte und denken aus Sicht der Cybersicherheit darüber nach – ganz klar sind diese Modelle sehr leistungsfähig. Unser Fokus liegt darauf, sicherzustellen, dass unsere Produkte sicher und zuverlässig sind und die Daten unserer Nutzer:innen geschützt bleiben“, so Ternus im Interview. Auch deshalb solle die Entscheidung über Produktneuheiten beim Menschen bleiben. „Die Entwicklung von Produkten ist eine zutiefst menschliche und persönliche Angelegenheit, etwas, das wir gerne tun.“

articles.title: Design and experience: How Essensai 067 crafts an open-air lifestyle and community destination
articles.text:
Design and experience: How Essensai 067 crafts an open-air lifestyle and community destination
In this photo essay from Whitefield, we showcase design highlights from Essensai 067 along with founder insights.
Launched in 2014, PhotoSparks is a weekly feature from YourStory, with photographs that celebrate the spirit of creativity and innovation. In the earlier 1,030 posts, we featured an art festival, cartoon gallery. world music festival, telecom expo, millets fair, climate change expo, wildlife conference, startup festival, Diwali rangoli, and jazz festival.
Does every large retail destination in a rapidly growing city have to be like a multi-storeyed air-conditioned mall? Essensai 067 in Whitefield does not believe so, and has found a unique positioning as an open-air lifestyle and community destination.
As shown in this photo essay, it combines dining, entertainment, shopping, wellness, and culture in a green and spacious setting Visitors can enjoy landscaped spaces and relaxed outdoor experiences rather than spending their time inside a boxed mall.
The space is also pet-friendly, unlike many other retail destinations and dining areas. The artworks and design encourage people to slow down and enjoy quality time, with a notable focus on sustainability, culture and community engagement.
Natural landscaping, solar energy, and climate-sensitive design send out subtle messages about environmental protection as well. The amphitheatre and open gathering spaces are host to live music, cultural performances, exhibitions, flea markets, and other community events.
Event programming has included garba nights, Christmas carnivals, qawaali, open-air movie nights, and pop-up markets. There was even a Kidzeprenuer Flea Market, where children aged 6–14 ran their own stalls over two days.
“The enthusiastic community response reinforces our belief that programming can give a neighbourhood destination a life beyond shopping and dining. Success is not just about how many people show up on a particular evening, but in how they begin to see the space as part of their own neighbourhood routine,” Haresh Mirpuri. MD of Sai Lakshmi Industries and Creative Director of Essensai 067, tells YourStory.
Interestingly, the name of the space is derived from a combination of the words essence, Sai Lakshmi Industries, Sai Baba, and the 067 postal code of the Whitefield neighbourhood.
“Whitefield has grown rapidly in terms of homes and offices. We felt there was an opportunity to create a different kind of neighbourhood experience: somewhere you could go for a morning walk, sit with a coffee, take a class, discover something being made, meet friends without making elaborate plans, or simply spend time outdoors,” Mirpuri observes.
That was the starting point for Essensai 067. “We wanted to bring nature, art, community and craft into the same conversation as local and international food, retail, wellness, and entertainment. These are not separate attractions assembled under one roof; they are different parts of how people want to live,” he adds.
As trends in retail and lifestyle, he points to the growing expectation for engaging experiences, variations in weekday and weekend activities, and active citizen participation. “People increasingly want to do something, learn something, meet the person behind a product, or become part of an experience,” Mirpuri describes.
“We designed the district to feel thoughtfully put together – offering commercial vitality, but also with a clear point of view. Curation matters as much as the individual offering,” he affirms.
A space is defined not just by its architecture or layout. “Its character develops through the people who visit, the brands and makers who become part of it, the experiences that take root, and the habits that form over time,” he adds.
“Any future location would need its own local understanding, programming and identity. The thinking should travel; the experience itself must belong to the neighbourhood,” Mirpuri explains, while referring to next steps.
In sum, Essensai 067 is aiming to build a destination that feels as dynamic and engaging as the city itself, while retaining the ease, openness and sense of familiarity of a neighbourhood space.
Mirpuri also offers tips for aspiring entrepreneurs in retail, food and entertainment. “Before deciding what a space should contain, understand who lives around it, how they spend their time, what they travel elsewhere for, and what is missing from their everyday lives,” he says.
“Build frequency before fame. It is easy to focus on a launch, a large event or a moment of visibility. The harder and more valuable task is giving people reasons to return,” he adds.
Curation can be more impactful than scale. “Not every destination needs the largest assortment or the most brands. It needs a clear point of view about what belongs there and why,” Mirpuri explains.
“Finally, allow the people you work with to retain their identity. Independent brands, artists, makers, and experience partners bring their own communities and points of view. The role of the destination is to host, curate and enable them—not flatten everything into a single house style,” he says.
In experience-led businesses, the physical space is only the beginning. “What matters is the relationship that develops between the place, its partners and the people who return to it. That relationship is built through consistency, listening and a willingness to keep evolving,” Mirpuri signs off.
Now what have you done today to pause in your busy schedule and harness your creative side for a better world?
(All photographs taken by Madanmohan Rao on location at Essensai 067.)

articles.title: Disney remonte le temps avec Ghost Rider, Elon Musk remonte l'Odyssey à sa sauce, et Cyberpunk 2077 s'invite dans vos navigateurs, c'est le récap pop culture de la semaine
articles.text:
Ghost Rider : le prochain film Marvel fait un choix qui n’a pas été fait depuis 15 ans
- Le prochain Ghost Rider sera le premier film Marvel Studios tourné en pellicule 35 mm depuis Thor et Captain America : First Avenger, en 2011.
- Réalisé par Shawn Levy avec Ryan Gosling pressenti dans le rôle de Johnny Blaze, le film doit entrer en tournage à New York en 2027.
- Le chef opérateur Linus Sandgren misera sur le grain et les teintes plus chaudes de l’argentique pour donner au film une esthétique plus brute.
Elon Musk lâche le premier épisode de sa vision de l’Odyssée pour « humilier Nolan »
- Elon Musk a relancé Grok Imagine pour créer une fresque IA présentée comme « historiquement exacte » inspirée du poème d’Homère, destinée à concurrencer l’adaptation de Christopher Nolan de L’Odyssée.
- Le projet s’inscrit dans une riposte culturelle personnelle : Musk a publiquement attaqué le casting de Nolan et affirmé que ces choix répondaient à des impératifs de diversité imposés par l’Académie.
- L’épisode inaugural de sept minutes, produit avec Wonder Studios, montre les avancées techniques de la génération vidéo par IA mais expose aussi des animations figées, un manque d’incarnation et des réactions critiques très partagées.
Cyberpunk 2077 est désormais jouable dans un navigateur, sans installation
- Un développeur indépendant, omonkey, a créé un portage non officiel de Cyberpunk 2077 jouable directement dans un navigateur web.
- Ce projet utilise WebGPU et WebAssembly pour exploiter les capacités graphiques des appareils compatibles, mais présente des limitations de performances et nécessite une connexion Internet robuste.
- Bien que cette version non officielle permette un accès gratuit, elle pourrait être retirée rapidement par CD Projekt RED en raison de sa nature illégale.

articles.title: 11.11 d'AliExpress : la Nintendo Switch 2 repasse sous son prix officiel
articles.text:
En plein mois du Black Friday, AliExpress lance ses soldes du 11.11, la fête des célibataires, alors que Nintendo vend sa Switch 2 seule 499,99 € depuis sa hausse de prix du 1er septembre. Avec le code FRD11100, AliExpress la propose à 420,88 € jusqu’au 12 novembre : une vraie baisse face au prix officiel, chez un vendeur de marketplace dont il faut vérifier les conditions de garantie.
Sortie en juin 2025, la Switch 2 reprend le principe hybride de sa devancière avec un écran de 7,9 pouces, 256 Go de stockage et des Joy-Con 2 qui se fixent par aimants. Sans jeu inclus, elle coûte aujourd’hui 499,99 € au prix conseillé par Nintendo. Avec le code FRD11100, la Nintendo Switch 2 en version européenne vendue sur AliExpress descend à 420,88 €, soit 79,11 € de moins. L’offre s’inscrit dans les soldes du 11.11 d’AliExpress et vise les joueurs qui attendaient une baisse après la hausse de septembre, à condition d’accepter une marketplace internationale.
La Nintendo Switch 2 passe à 420,88 € au lieu de 499,99 € au prix conseillé chez AliExpress, grâce au code FRD11100 à saisir avant le paiement.
Pourquoi choisir la Nintendo Switch 2 ?
- Un écran pensé pour le jeu nomade : Sa dalle LCD de 7,9 pouces affiche du 1080p jusqu’à 120 Hz avec VRR, ce qui rend les jeux exigeants nettement plus fluides en mode portable. Sur un téléviseur, la console grimpe jusqu’à la 4K à 60 images par seconde.
- Une ludothèque qui ne repart pas de zéro : La console fait tourner les jeux Switch 1, et certains profitent d’une mise à jour « Switch 2 Edition ». Votre collection Switch 1 garde donc une seconde vie.
- Des Joy-Con 2 repensés : Fixés par aimants, plus grands et mieux en main, ils peuvent aussi servir de souris grâce à leur capteur optique. La fonction GameChat permet en outre de discuter à la voix via le micro intégré.
Du canapé au train, une console qui change de cadence
Sur un trajet, l’écran plus grand et plus fluide fait la différence : les jeux tournent souvent en 1080p à 60 images par seconde en mode portable. Le revers tient à l’autonomie, que Nintendo annonce entre 2 et 6,5 heures. Dans notre test de la Nintendo Switch 2, nous avions relevé environ 3 heures sur Tears of the Kingdom, et 5 à 6 heures sur des titres plus légers. Branchée à un téléviseur compatible, elle délivre jusqu’à la 4K à 60 images par seconde ou du 1440p à 120 Hz.
Elle s’adresse d’abord aux joueurs Switch 1 qui veulent garder leur ludothèque tout en profitant d’une image plus nette, et aux familles qui alternent salon et jeu nomade. Avec 534 grammes, elle reste lourde pour de longues sessions tenue en main. Les amateurs d’HDR seront aussi déçus en mobilité, l’écran n’offrant pas de véritable rendu HDR en mode portable. Enfin, à 420,88 € sans jeu, il faut prévoir le budget d’un premier titre.
Switch 2, Switch Lite ou Steam Deck OLED : ce que vous payez vraiment
La Switch 2 n’est pas la seule porte d’entrée vers le jeu nomade. Dans notre comparatif des meilleures consoles portables, la Switch Lite reste notre meilleur rapport qualité-prix, plus légère et plus compacte, tandis que le Steam Deck OLED séduit par sa dalle OLED à 90 Hz et son autonomie améliorée. La Switch 2 y figure en quatrième position, saluée pour son écran, ses performances et ses finitions, mais avec un tarif jugé très élevé. Cette offre atténue ce dernier reproche, sans le faire disparaître.
✅ Les points forts
- Écran LCD de 7,9 pouces en 1080p à 120 Hz avec VRR
- Rétrocompatibilité avec les jeux Switch 1
- 256 Go de stockage intégrés
- Joy-Con 2 aimantés, utilisables comme une souris
- 79,11 € sous le prix conseillé de 499,99 €
❌ Les limites
- Autonomie d’environ 3 heures sur les jeux exigeants
- Pas de véritable HDR en mode portable
- Console seule, aucun jeu inclus
- Vendeur de marketplace : garantie et version expédiée à vérifier
Lancé pour le 11.11, le code FRD11100 est annoncé jusqu’au 12 novembre : contrôlez que le panier affiche 420,88 € avant de valider votre Switch 2 chez AliExpress.
À 420,88 €, la Switch 2 repasse sous son prix conseillé de 499,99 €, et même sous son prix de lancement de 469,99 €. Ce n’est pas pour autant son plus bas sur AliExpress : fin août, juste avant la hausse, une vente flash limitée à 20 unités l’avait fait descendre à 359,57 € le temps d’une soirée. L’offre du 11.11 court en revanche sur près de deux semaines. Pour un joueur qui attendait de passer à la nouvelle génération, c’est un point d’entrée sérieux.
Elle convient surtout à ceux qui possèdent déjà des jeux Switch 1 et comptent alterner téléviseur et jeu nomade. Ceux qui jouent rarement loin d’une prise, ou qui refusent les aléas d’un vendeur international, préféreront un revendeur français, quitte à payer davantage. Avant de valider, prenez le temps de lire la fiche : la mention « version européenne, garantie locale » et l’indication d’une version « nouvelle ou précédente selon disponibilité » méritent une question au vendeur.

articles.title: "Ghost students" stole millions in federal aid until data patterns gave them away
articles.text:
Connecting the dots: Federal prosecutors in Nebraska, Virginia and New Jersey have charged five people in a student aid fraud scheme that used AI to fake coursework and class attendance. The case also led to a cryptocurrency seizure in Kenya. It shows how AI is making fake students harder to spot, just as the automated identity checks meant to stop them raise new concerns about real students being wrongly flagged.
Unusual patterns in federal student aid data led the Justice Department to charge five people and seize more than $750,000 in cryptocurrency tied to a network associated with Kenyan nationals. The charges are the first results of a broader federal effort, which the department calls Operation Ghostbusters, to crack down on "ghost student" fraud.
The scheme used stolen identities to enroll fake students in colleges, and relied partly on AI to keep those students looking active long enough to collect aid.
The case began at the Department of Education's Office of Inspector General, which first spotted the fraud patterns. The FBI then worked out how many accounts were involved and followed the money into US and foreign bank accounts and crypto wallets.
Theophani K. Stamos, First Assistant US Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia, said at a press conference that data analysis "identified unusual, suspicious patterns of behavior." The FBI said those patterns showed coordinated fraud involving the FAFSA, which Stamos said gave investigators "a solid basis and a solid lead to open further inquiries that have led to indictments."
Some of the money trails were large. One defendant used accounts at several financial institutions to receive more than 700 fraudulent aid refund deposits worth about $1.44 million, the Justice Department said. Inside Higher Ed reported that another person received more than $1 million in deposits linked to more than 300 fake student accounts.
The FBI has identified more than $32 million in losses from similar ghost student schemes, officials said, and believes the true total is "substantially higher."
The wider exposure may be far bigger. The Education Department has "identified over 830,000 potentially fraudulent federal student aid accounts created by using this PII of US citizens," officials said. If every one of those accounts turns out to be a ghost student, the Justice Department estimates losses close to $130 million. Stamos's office has sent "approximately 50 referrals to 26 FBI field offices across the country."
The scheme starts with purchased personal data. The usual targets are people who finished high school and went straight to work. Because they have no college record, the Education Department has nothing to cross-check the applications against. The fraudsters file FAFSA forms and apply to universities and community colleges.
If a fake student is accepted, the aid goes first to the school for tuition and fees, and whatever is left is sent to bank accounts the fraudsters control. Dozens of Americans have opened accounts to serve as money mules, the Justice Department said.
AI helps keep the fake students from being detected. It fills out applications, completes coursework and, in some cases, creates the appearance of a person attending online classes.
"It looks like the ghost student is actually completing the class," said Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department's National Fraud Enforcement Division. "Some even create the appearance of a fake student in an online classroom to trick schools into believing a real person is present. The goal is to keep the ghost student in school for as long as possible, semester after semester after semester."
The Justice Department believes the scheme has been running since at least 2021 and has grown more sophisticated as AI has opened new ways to steal loans. McDonald credited fraud-detection measures introduced by the Trump administration for the arrests and called the Kenyan seizure "the first international seizure of its kind in Kenya."
Victims often find out only years later, when the government tries to collect on the loans. By then their credit may already be damaged. "The Department of Education does a great job to help unravel that mess, but it is a mess that no one should have to endure," McDonald said.
Under identity verification rules the Education Department added this year, applicants hold a government-issued ID up to their camera in real time while automated systems review it. A senior department official told Inside Higher Ed the systems are "similar to the ones used by financial services companies like banks." Each applicant then gets a risk rating, and anyone rated "high risk" is rejected.
After that, it is up to the school to check whether the application was real. Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson, vice chair of the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, argued that this kind of automation can stop fraud without adding staff. "The computers help us find it, and we keep the money in the agency," he said.
The software has already had problems. In August, the department confirmed that a technical issue from June 29 to July 6 kept fraud evaluation results from being attached to certain FAFSA forms. Those applications were later reprocessed. Advocates also warn that false flags put more work on schools and can delay aid. MorraLee Keller, a senior consultant for the National College Attainment Network, told Inside Higher Ed that "a lot of low-economic kids may not have secured, for example, a driver's license." Students who correct their FAFSA can also be screened again, which means a false rejection could hold up their money.
The administration says it expects few real students to be flagged, but it hasn't put a number on it. In April, Melanie Storey, president of the National Association of Student Financial Aid Administrators, asked the department on an association podcast "to quantify the volume of in-person verification that will remain." Aaron Lemon-Strauss, executive director of the FAFSA program, replied, "I'm not going to be able to give you a number yet." For students who "accidentally get caught in the net," he urged universities to stay vigilant.

articles.title: Calendário astronômico: novembro traz distância histórica da Terra, fim do Mercúrio retrógrado e chuva de meteoros
articles.text:
Novembro começa neste domingo trazendo o fim do último Mercúrio retrógrado do ano, uma chuva de meteoros, Urano em seu melhor momento de observação e uma Superlua. Enquanto isso, a exploração espacial atinge um marco inédito: a sonda Voyager 1 vai atingir a distância de um dia-luz da Terra. E tem muito mais!
Lembrando que todas as datas e horários fornecidos têm como referência um observador em Brasília (DF) e podem variar ligeiramente de acordo com a localidade. Para acompanhar com precisão, a dica é usar aplicativos como Star Walk, Stellarium ou SkySafari, que mostram a posição exata dos objetos celestes com base em onde você está.
Calendário astronômico de novembro
9 de novembro: Aniversário de Carl Sagan. Data dedicada a celebrar as contribuições do astrofísico e o legado de divulgação científica deixado por ele.
13 de novembro: Fim do movimento retrógrado de Mercúrio. Como a órbita do planeta é curta, ele completa uma volta ao redor do Sol a cada 88 dias e acaba “ultrapassando” a Terra com frequência. Por causa desse ritmo, três ou quatro vezes por ano ele parece andar para trás no céu por cerca de três semanas.
18 de novembro: Pico da chuva de meteoros Leônidas. Com a Lua 61% iluminada no início da noite, mas se pondo antes do horário de maior visibilidade, o evento poderá ser observado tanto no Hemisfério Sul quanto no Norte.
25 de novembro: Urano em oposição. O planeta fica em sua melhor posição de observação no ano. Embora seja tecnicamente possível enxergá-lo a olho nu em céus livres de poluição luminosa, o uso de binóculos ou telescópios é essencial para a maioria dos observadores.
25 de novembro: Superlua do Castor – em referência ao período em que os animais construíam barragens e armazenavam comida para o inverno. Outra explicação diz que o nome veio de caçadores que coletavam peles de castor para se aquecer nos meses frios. Na ocasião, a Lua se torna cheia próxima ao perigeu, ponto da órbita mais próximo da Terra. Assim, o disco lunar parecerá ligeiramente maior e até 14% mais brilhante que uma lua cheia comum.
Missões espaciais atingem marcos importantes este mês
Em algum momento deste mês, a sonda Hera chega a Didymos-Dimorphos para realizar o primeiro encontro com um sistema binário de asteroides. A espaçonave da Agência Espacial Europeia (ESA) estudará as consequências do impacto da missão DART, da NASA, e ajudará a aprimorar técnicas de defesa planetária, liberando dois cubesats antes de iniciar suas operações científicas em 2027.
Outro destaque é a entrada da BepiColombo na órbita de Mercúrio. A missão conjunta da ESA e da Agência de Exploração Aeroespacial do Japão (JAXA) se dividirá entre o Orbitador Planetário de Mercúrio (MPO) e o Orbitador Magnetosférico de Mercúrio (MIO) para investigar a superfície, o interior e o campo magnético do planeta.
Ainda em novembro, aproximadamente no dia 15, a sonda Voyager 1, da NASA, alcançará a distância de um dia-luz da Terra. Ativa quase 50 anos após o lançamento em 1977, a espaçonave estará a 25,9 bilhões de quilômetros do nosso planeta, fazendo a luz levar um dia inteiro para cruzar essa distância.
Flávia Correia é jornalista do Olhar Digital, cobrindo Ciência e Espaço.

articles.title: Pixel 11 Pro Fold: Sturdy rectangle in a wide wide world | TechCrunch
articles.text:
It’s strange to write this review when the world is focused on the passport-sized iPhone Duo, and China-based companies are busy releasing wide foldables with a similar design. Google, however, stuck to its guns this year and produced a Pixel 11 Pro Fold, which is pretty much similar to last year’s foldable.
The changes involve a lighter design, a brighter display, better wireless charging, and an updated camera sensor. The new olive color looks subtle but gorgeous, so that’s a bonus. However, with all the options out there, the device might not attract people who might be looking to buy their first foldable — unless they’re serious Pixel fans.
Nonetheless, I have enjoyed using the device because the Pixel 11 Pro Fold’s cameras are competent enough, even if they aren’t a match for the Pixel 11 Pro’s setup, and the screen is nice to use despite the very visible crease.
Design
The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is 5mm thick when unfolded (vs 5.2mm of the Pixel 10 Pro Fold) and 10.1mm thick when folded (vs 10.8 mm of the Pixel 10 Pro Fold). This one is for the spec sheet because you might not feel as much difference. Despite this, the phone is not as thin as a device like the Honor V6 Magic.
The difference you might notice — if you hold both this year’s and last year’s foldables — is that the new device is 19 grams lighter. But if you are buying a new device or switching from another foldable, it’s barely noticeable.
The Pixel 10 Pro Fold was already a sturdy device. With this year’s version, the company claims to have increased durability by three times. Plus, there is a new glass-ceramic cover and a glass-fiber composite back cover to take up any impact. My Pixel 10 fell a few times from the table and from my pocket, but there wasn’t any visible dent or scratch. Well done, Google.
One drawback of a strong hinge is that you can’t unfold the 11 Pro Fold with one hand, and that’s by design.
The outer display is ever so slightly bigger, but the more observable change is the 3,600-nit display that is an upgrade from last year’s 3,000-nit peak display. This means that you can use the phone in bright conditions better.
Google’s foldable still has a very visible crease in an age where phone makers like Oppo and Honor have managed to reduce the visibility significantly. The crease is more pronounced in bright light, given there is no reflective display on the device.
On the back, there is the new HiLight indicator, which still lights up only for calls from your favourite contacts, and when you are talking with Gemini hands-free. There isn’t much to talk about this feature beyond that.
Software and AI
Reading and watching videos on a foldable is still fun, though a wide foldable might show an edge on videos. The multitasking is good, but you can only open two apps side by side. Some apps that are tuned for foldable are great to use. For instance, Gmail, being a Google app, lets you see your inbox on one side and a particular email on the other. This can help you get through emails faster. However, Slack doesn’t have this split view, and it’s frustrating because we have been through many cycles of Android foldables with apps still not suited for the expanded screen.
Given how quick Apple developer system moves, Android might feel it’s lagging in foldable experiences after the iPhone Duo is out. The camps are divided as to how apps look on Duo’s unfolded phone, but developers are rapidly updating their apps to fit the unfolded screen.
The bubbles, which let you access apps in floating windows and minimize them in a taskbar, are a good idea. That way, you can temporarily look at information in an app without having to make it a full-sized window.
Gemini updates this year were muted. The company built on its idea of Magic Cue to give timely suggestions in different apps. As I mentioned in my Pixel 11 Pro XL review, Rambler was my favorite feature to use in the new Pixel lineups. I could easily reply to emails and texts, and take notes, without involving texting on a wide keyboard.
Camera
Foldables have mostly had inferior cameras to their candybar counterparts for years now. While this year is no different, Google continuing to use the “Pro” moniker for its foldable feels like a disservice. The Pixel 11 Pro Fold cameras are good, but they aren’t Pixel 11 Pro XL good.
There are a few positives with the new version. There is an updated main sensor, still a 48-megapixel one, that lets more light in for photos with better detail. Google has also updated its models to support 30x Super Res Zoom, up from 20x Super Res Zoom.
Even if Google wouldn’t include the same ultrawide and telephoto sensors as the slab Pro devices, I wish they would use the same main sensor on the Fold as the rectangle phone. The telephoto and ultrawide sensors are similar to last year’s device, so there is barely any improvement in images taken from them.
In terms of software features, there is Looks, which can change the tone of an image with different presets, and Magic Capture, which can pick the best frames from a video — useful for when you have pets or kids.
Price
At $1,899, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold is for someone who likes Pixels and wants a foldable, given it’s barely $100 less than the new iPhone Duo and the same price as the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8, which are both wide-format phones. In the U.S., the taller Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra starts at $2,099.
In Europe, companies like Xiaomi and Honor are going to release their foldables, too. So Google’s foldable is going to face a lot of competition.

articles.title: Las 7 mejores películas de terror de 2026 (hasta ahora)
articles.text:
El año 2026 demostró que las películas de terror se han convertido en parte esencial de un año prolífico en el mundo cinematográfico. Pero mucho más, que el género recuperó su sitial de honor como uno de los más rentables, entretenidos y atractivos de la industria. En específico, porque del triunfo de Los pecadores y Weapons el año pasado, las historias espeluznantes también son las favoritas de la crítica. Algo que ha permitido aumentar su calidad, impacto y el interés a su alrededor.
Todo lo anterior ha sido consecuencia de un proceso más o menos largo. El cine de terror ha experimentado una transformación radical en la última década. Además, atraviesa una década dorada marcada por el nacimiento del llamado terror elevado o terror psicológico de autor. Todo gracias al repunte de toda una nueva generación. Productoras independientes como A24 y Blumhouse, junto a directores como Ari Aster, Jordan Peele y Robert Eggers, redefinieron el género. Eso al alejarlo de los sustos fáciles y enfocarlo en historias más profundas y perturbadoras.
De modo que las películas de terror contemporáneas utilizan el miedo como una metáfora para explorar diversos temas. De traumas familiares, el racismo, la desconexión social hasta el deterioro mental. Por lo que atraen tanto a la crítica especializada como a un público masivo que busca experiencias cinematográficas más complejas y viscerales. Algo que quedó demostrado a lo largo de este interesante año, cuyas mejores películas te dejamos a continuación.
Resident Evil (Zach Cregger)
¿Te sorprende encontrar la más reciente adaptación del juego de Capcom en la lista? Piénsalo de nuevo. La cinta de Zach Creeger convierte la conocida premisa de una epidemia zombi en una survivor movie de enorme calidad. Tanto, que logró una espectacular aprobación del 96 % en Rotten Tomatoes gracias a su asfixiante fidelidad a las raíces de supervivencia del material original. El director, reconocido por su manejo de la tensión claustrofóbica, traslada la acción a los rincones más oscuros de la mítica Raccoon City.
Para eso, la trama sigue a Bryan Hodukavich (Austin Abrams), un personaje novedoso que, aun así, se convierte en el centro del argumento. ¿El motivo? Ser la encarnación de cualquier jugador que haya jugado la experiencia para videoconsolas. De modo que este mensajero médico común y corriente termina atrapado en una carrera contrarreloj para entregar un tratamiento vital. Eso en medio de un brote viral devastador.
La genialidad de la premisa radica en que se desmarca por completo de la acción de las adaptaciones pasadas. Por lo que Resident Evil prioriza la escasez de recursos, el aislamiento extremo y el miedo. Una delicia para fanáticos que logró cautivar al público generalista y convertirse en una de las grandes películas de terror del año.
Backrooms (Kane Parsons)
El fenómeno viral del terror analógico y digna heredera de las creepypastas online es una de las grandes películas de terror del año. De la mano del estudio A24, superó récords de taquilla con una recaudación global que superó los 400 millones de dólares. Con apenas 20 años de edad, el director Kane Parsons expandió su propio universo de espacios liminales nacido originalmente en YouTube. La película utiliza las interminables y deprimentes oficinas alfombradas de iluminación fluorescente parpadeante para sumergirnos en una crisis de horror existencial.
Para eso, la historia sigue a Clark (Chiwetel Ejiofor), un atormentado dueño de una tienda de muebles que descubre una misteriosa compuerta en su sótano. El guion entrelaza hábilmente la claustrofobia física de los pasillos infinitos con una punzante metáfora sobre la obsesión y el aislamiento de la era digital. Pero además, convertir la idea de un espacio ilimitado y terrorífico en una idea que se hace cada vez más angustiosa. De las películas de terror que sorprendieron en este 2026.
Obsesión (Curry Barker)
Este microproyecto, convertido en un hit mundial, rompió esquemas. Mucho más, al convertir a su jovencísimo director Curry Barker en una de las grandes figuras del terror mundial. En especial, al recaudar la impresionante cifra de 522 millones de dólares de taquilla. Pero además, convertir la historia retorcida de un deseo cumplido en una exploración sobre la violencia sexual y el miedo. Todo, en un estudio minimalista acerca de lo sobrenatural.
Para eso, Barker demuestra un control total sobre el ritmo narrativo. Por lo que equilibra de forma brillante el humor negro más ácido con momentos de pura perversión psicológica y terror doméstico. La película funciona a la perfección como una disección de la cultura del acoso y las fijaciones modernas. Lo que la convirtió en una de las grandes sorpresas del cine de terror del año.
28 años después: El templo de los huesos (Nia DaCosta)
Aunque pasó desapercibida en la taquilla, esta cinta de Nia DaCosta sorprende por su originalidad y su puesta en escena. Cuarta entrega de la icónica saga de zombis iniciada por Danny Boyle, expande con éxito la mitología postapocalíptica del Reino Unido. La trama nos traslada varias décadas después del brote original. Todo para seguir los pasos de Spike (Alfie Williams), protagonista de la anterior y esta vez capturado por una brutal y desquiciada banda criminal. Esta última, conocida como Los Jimmys, liderada por un perturbador fanático religioso interpretado magistralmente por Jack O’Connell.
Al mismo tiempo, el veterano actor Ralph Fiennes ofrece una de las mejores actuaciones de su carrera en el papel del doctor Ian Kelson. Un personaje cuyas investigaciones científicas con un infectado de clase alfa añaden una capa de inesperada melancolía y humanidad a la historia. DaCosta aprovecha los escenarios desolados para tejer una potente fábula sobre el colapso social y la inminente pérdida de la humanidad frente a la barbarie. Para la historia de las películas de terror de este año.
Insaciable (Natalie Erika James)
Aunque no hayas escuchado de esta película de terror, inclúyela en tu lista de lo mejor del año. En especial, porque este incómodo body horror transforma la obsesión moderna por la delgadez en una pesadilla sobrenatural. La trama sigue a Hana (Midori Francis), una estudiante de medicina con una obsesión: encajar en los implacables estándares estéticos actuales. Por lo que recurre a unas misteriosas píldoras adelgazantes.
Cuando el costoso suministro se agota, Hana utiliza sus conocimientos de laboratorio para replicar la fórmula. Lo que lleva a descubrir con horror que el ingrediente activo detrás de su milagrosa pérdida de peso son cenizas de cadáveres humanos. Miedo y crítica estética en una misma película para lo mejor de 2026.
Leviticus (Adrian Chiarella)
Esta joya del cine de terror independiente australiano es una de las películas de terror del año que quizás te pasó desapercibida. Dirigida por Adrian Chiarella, la trama sigue de cerca a dos adolescentes atrapados en un entorno profundamente hostil. Una además, por completo fuera de lo común. La entidad posee la habilidad de moldear su apariencia física y convertirse en la viva imagen de la persona que su víctima más desea. Lo que fuerza a los jóvenes a enfrentarse a su mutua e inconfesable atracción.
Chiarella entrelaza con una sutileza asombrosa los códigos del romance queer y el drama de autodescubrimiento con el horror de monstruos más clásico y descarnado. Con un elenco encabezado por Joe Bird, Stacy Clausen y Mia Wasikowska, la película destaca por sus atmósferas opresivas y un diseño visual que evoca una pesadilla constante. Ideal para los que buscan un giro poco convencional en su lista de mejores películas de terror del año.
Posesión infernal: En llamas (Sébastien Vaniček)
La legendaria franquicia Evil Dead regresa con una nueva entrega a cargo del cineasta francés Sébastien Vaniček. Una decisión que inyecta una dosis masiva de brutalidad e intensidad física a la mítica saga creada por Sam Raimi. Para eso, la historia sigue a Alice, una viuda interpretada por Souheila Yacoub, que busca apoyo en la casa de campo aislada de sus suegros.
El drama familiar se desmorona violentamente cuando el descubrimiento de un libro maldito desata una implacable fuerza demoníaca. Una además, que comienza a poseer a los integrantes de la familia uno por uno. Fiel al legado de la saga, Vaniček renuncia casi por completo a los efectos digitales. Por lo que sumerge al espectador en un festival de efectos prácticos y gore de la vieja escuela. Pero además, explora las transformaciones de los deadites desde una cuidadosa puesta en escena. Todo, en una inteligente exploración de la culpa y el duelo. Una de las grandes películas de terror que deberías ver este año.

articles.title: USAF successfully tests dropping SpaceX Starfall cargo drop pods from space — 2,200-pound capsule drops military supplies in the Pacific to test StarCraft-like supply drops
articles.text:
USAF successfully tests dropping SpaceX Starfall cargo drop pods from space — 2,200-pound capsule drops military supplies in the Pacific to test StarCraft-like supply drops
The U.S. is developing the Rocket Cargo capability for the entire military.
The Air Force Research Lab (AFRL), the research and development arm of the US Air Force, has successfully tested Rocket Cargo capabilities, which would allow military units to resupply via cargo pods dropped from space. According to the AFRL’s X post, the cargo pods, which were onboard a SpaceX Starfall capsule, launched from the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station as part of the Bandwagon-5 “rideshare” mission carried by a Falcon 9 rocket. The capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean for this test, with the unit containing mission equipment like MREs, bottled water, a SATCOM-enabled tracker, spare batteries, and other equipment. The AFRL also fit-checked a UNI-PAC III life raft to see if it would fit inside the Starfall capsule for a potential test in the future.
The mission is a test of Rocket Cargo’s point-to-point delivery (P2D) capabilities, which should allow forces to resupply virtually anywhere in the world without needing to risk other assets like aircraft and aircrews, especially in areas where there is active combat.
“This was a critical achievement to demonstrate the potential of Rocket Cargo delivery for point-to-point rapid global mobility for the Future Force," AFRL Technology Transition Office director Adam Remaly said in a statement. "The cross-discipline collaborations and ability to unleash the speed of our defense industrial base are key to maximizing capability and winning the future.”
The Starfall capsule, which looks like a hockey puck, measures about 10 feet across and has a capacity of up to 2,200 pounds. It uses a carbon fiber heat shield to protect its contents during reentry and uses compressed gas thrusters for attitude control in flight. Finally, it deploys a parachute system to slow down the entire system for landing. While 2,200 pounds might already seem like a substantial capacity, the Air Force is reportedly hoping that it could increase the limit in the order of tens of tons, potentially allowing it to resupply ammunition, weapon systems, and even deploy vehicles from space. This would have to wait for the larger SpaceX Starship rockets, which are still in development, though.
Even though the latest test seemingly relies mostly on SpaceX technologies, it’s not the only company developing that capability for the U.S. military. Sierra Space, a subsidiary of the Sierra Nevada Corporation, is also working on the Ghost reentry vehicle and has already conducted test drops of the system from heights of 35,000 and 68,500 feet.
The capability to resupply troops across long distances without needing to rely on a long logistical tail is crucial for the U.S., especially as it faces a potential adversary in the Pacific. It’s also for this reason that the U.S. Navy has been experimenting with 3D-printing technologies, allowing it to print parts onboard carriers and at forward bases instead of waiting for shipments from across the ocean.

articles.title: New Zelda and GTA represent a games industry that no longer exists
articles.text:
This is The Stepback, a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more on the biggest game releases of the year, follow Andrew Webster. The Stepback arrives in our subscribers’ inboxes on Sunday at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepbackhere.
New Zelda and GTA represent a games industry that no longer exists
The two biggest games of the year launch in November, offering some reprieve from a terrible year.
New Zelda and GTA represent a games industry that no longer exists
The two biggest games of the year launch in November, offering some reprieve from a terrible year.
How it started
The two biggest games of 2026 are set to launch just a few weeks apart in November.
On the one side you have the behemoth that is Grand Theft Auto VI, an experience 13 years in the making, and the sequel to one of the best-selling games in history. Its predecessor, GTA V, has sold a staggering 230 million copies since it launched in 2013, and was re-released across three generations of consoles. Developer Rockstar is a pioneer in the realm of open-world games, dating back to GTA III, and the scale and ambitions of those worlds have steadily grown since then. With GTA V and later Red Dead Redemption 2, the studio’s ideas reached a new level of realism. And the sixth GTA looks poised to eclipse them both, which has created an unprecedented level of demand.
Analyst firm Circana estimates that 29 percent of gamers in the US intend to buy the game, with demand so large it could boost flagging console sales. “Many consumers who have yet to upgrade to a current-generation console may choose to purchase a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series specifically to play the title,” analyst Mat Piscatella says in a statement. GTA VI’s reach is so vast that almost every other major game launched early to avoid it.
The one exception is Nintendo. The company’s tentpole release for the holidays, and its next major exclusive for the Switch 2, is a lavish remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.
The release is notable for a few reasons. For one thing, it’s an attempt from Nintendo to modernize one of the most influential and beloved games in its long history. The original Ocarina of Time was the world’s first introduction to a 3D iteration of Hyrule, which, in turn, made it an early glimpse at what was possible in three-dimensional spaces, laying a blueprint for countless games that came afterward. Nintendo has since expanded on that, turning Switch-era adventures Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom into wide-open adventures designed for player creativity. They went on to become some of the best-selling games for Nintendo’s most successful console.
Ocarina of Time’s launch also comes just ahead of a live-action Zelda movie in 2027, which could catapult the franchise to a new level of prominence. That’s why Nintendo is seemingly the only company unafraid of competing with GTA.
These aren’t just two blockbuster games – they’re two series with the pull to make this a real cultural moment, akin to “Barbenheimer” but for video games. They’re the kind of launches that make it onto Saturday Night Live and have NBA players worried.
It’s just too bad about the rest of the industry.
How it’s going
These major November releases are something of a mirage, two outliers that stand out amid the wreckage that is the rest of the video game industry. While there have been plenty of major releases and great games this year, the main theme of 2026 has been just how dire things have become. Layoffs, studio closures, unpopular business models, the ever-looming threat of AI, and massive increases in hardware costs have combined to create an ominous cloud over the medium.
Here is just a snapshot of what the year has been like: Xbox is in the middle of a “reset” that involves laying off thousands of developers, shutting down some studios, and gutting others; Fortnite developer Epic cut more than 1,000 jobs due to a sharp downturn in the live-service games space, and it’s currently going all-in on vibe coding; Sony is also struggling, slashing jobs at Destiny developer Bungie, watching console sales plummet as costs skyrocket, and raising the ire of gamers by moving on from physical media; and meanwhile, major publishers like EA and Ubisoft are in their own dramatic states of upheaval.
And the bad news hasn’t really let up. Just last week, EA shut down beloved studio BioWare and canceled the next Mass Effect game, and this week Sony studio Sucker Punch cut staff despite the success of last year’s Ghost of Yōtei. Every day, it seems, brings some new unwelcome development.
What happens next
Clearly, things are changing for the video game industry; they have to change. What that future looks like, though, remains unclear. The next generation of game consoles is being threatened by exorbitant prices, and all the while the rise of AI-powered tools is sending ripples across the industry, threatening the established order between players and creators as games are ported to every platform imaginable. “These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models,” Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said in a recent memo. But how that plays out remains to be seen.
It’s not all doom and gloom. There have been rare success stories, where studios like FromSoftware and Remedy have managed to carve out a sustainable existence in a turbulent field. But for the most part, the established norms that have been part of the blockbuster games industry for years are going away. Big games are too expensive to make, hardware is too expensive to buy (and the cost is only going up), and somewhere, something has to give.
It’s tempting to look at Zelda and GTA as answers to these problems. After all, if Nintendo and Rockstar are doing so well, there must be a solution out there. But they’re also two very specific cases that are essentially impossible to replicate. Nintendo maintains ownership over all aspects of its platform, from the hardware to the games, and it has taken a careful and largely risk-averse approach that has allowed it to weather the current storm and create a growing entertainment empire. Rockstar, meanwhile, is the rare example of being too big to fail. GTA V was so massive for so long — Circana says it was among the top 20 best-selling games in the US for 13 straight years — that it allowed the studio to build up both an unprecedented amount of anticipation and, it seems, a game big enough to match it.
In that way, Zelda and GTA are throwbacks to a time when major games were sure bets. Their duelling releases are fascinating both because these games are so impactful, but also because, with all of the impending upheaval, the industry might never see a moment like this again.
By the way
- The Ocarina of Time remake makes some smart modern tweaks to the formula, which you can learn about in our hands-on with the game.
- While the wait has been long for GTA VI, it seems there’s a good chance its inevitable sequel won’t spend so many years in development.
- There’s one other notable game that was unafraid to launch in November: Moomin: Midsummer Madness.
Read this
- Rockstar is very secretive, but you can get a sense of what went into GTA VI’s protracted development from these cover stories in Edge magazine and Businessweek.
- Ocarina of Time is an especially interesting game in 2026 because of how much Zelda has changed since it first debuted. For more on that, here’s our interview from 2023 with Tears of the Kingdom director Hidemaro Fujibayashi.

articles.title: Building Obsolescence-Resilient Product Lifecycles - EE Times
articles.text:
Artificial intelligence is reshaping the semiconductor industry, and the effects reach well beyond the data center. As memory manufacturers prioritize capacity and investment for AI-driven products, some DDR3 and DDR4 devices used in long-life systems are facing reduced availability and earlier end-of-life announcements than many designers expected. For engineers building products expected to operate for decades, semiconductor obsolescence is not just a procurement challenge. It is a fundamental design, qualification, and lifecycle-management issue.
Aerospace, defense, transportation, industrial, and medical systems are often designed around long service lives, while the semiconductor technologies within them may have significantly shorter commercial lifespans. When a critical component reaches end-of-life (EOL), engineers may face difficult choices: secure sufficient inventory, redesign the system around a replacement device, or maintain the original design.
Obsolescence cannot always be avoided, but its impact can be better managed when lifecycle considerations are built into the design and program planning process from the outset.
Understanding the lifecycle challenge
The semiconductor industry runs on technology cycles far shorter than the working lives of the systems that use its devices. A component can remain technically ideal for an application long after it stops being commercially attractive to its original manufacturer.
For long-life sectors, the problem is compounded by the cost of change: modifying a validated design can trigger extensive testing, requalification, and recertification.
Rank parts by what losing them would cost
Lifecycle planning starts by distinguishing components by their importance to the overall system. An EOL notice for a readily replaceable device may have limited consequences, while losing a highly integrated or difficult-to-qualify component can ripple across the entire program.
Assess each component on its role in the system, the availability of technically suitable alternatives, qualification requirements, expected program lifetime, and the consequences of changing the hardware or software around it.
AI investment can affect legacy technologies
Much of today’s semiconductor investment is directed towards artificial intelligence and high-performance computing. Although these developments are concentrated at the leading edge, their effects extend into older technology generations.
Memory provides a useful example. As manufacturers prioritize products such as DDR5, GDDR6, HBM3 and LPDDR5, production capacity and investment can move away from earlier generations. Yet DDR3, DDR4 and other legacy technologies remain part of many industrial, medical, aerospace and other long-life systems.
Lifecycle planning therefore needs to cover the wider semiconductor ecosystem, not only processors, microcontrollers and FPGAs. Memory and supporting devices matter just as much to long-term availability.
Memory migration is rarely straightforward
Memory also demonstrates why identifying a replacement is not simply a matter of finding a device with the same capacity. Parameters such as data width, speed, temperature range, package, die configuration, and other characteristics can affect compatibility.
Moving between generations can introduce architectural and qualification considerations. Even an increase in capacity may require assessment if the original design was qualified around a particular device configuration.
Capturing these parameters during the original design and maintaining the information as part of the product lifecycle record can make future assessments more straightforward.
Plan around the program, not only the EOL notice
When a component reaches EOL, a last-time buy may appear to be the obvious response. However, this is not necessarily practical for a program requiring another 10, 15, or 20 years of support. The required quantity may require significant capital, while storage, inventory management, and changing demand add further considerations.
A longer-term approach starts with the program itself. Expected production volumes, service-life requirements, installed-base support, and the criticality of individual components can all influence the appropriate strategy. 
Depending on the circumstances, this may involve inventory planning, continued authorized manufacturing, redesign, or a combination of approaches. The important point is to consider these options before time pressure narrows the choices. 
Protect the supply chain, not only the design
Once a part is discontinued, independent and gray-market sellers fill the gap, bringing the risk of counterfeit, recycled, or poorly stored devices. For high-reliability and safety-critical systems, buying from authorized sources with full traceability to the original manufacturer, such as fully authorized distributors like Rochester Electronics that meet SAE AS6496, is the most dependable way to avoid that risk.
The value of technical dialogue
Lifecycle management is also an information-sharing exercise. Engineering teams know their product architecture and program requirements, while semiconductor and lifecycle specialists can provide insight into availability, manufacturing capability, and technology changes. 
Rochester Electronics works across both authorized distribution and licensed manufacturing. Where authorized finished devices remain available, they provide a source for continued support. When finished devices are no longer available, licensed manufacturing from authorized wafer and die offers another route to keep selected legacy devices in supply.
Rochester’s technical team works with local sales teams and customers to review bills of materials, understand program timelines, and examine component lifetimes, from a discussion around an individual device to analysis of hundreds of line items.
The earlier these conversations take place, the more options remain open. Regular communication also helps ensure that changes to forecasts, program timelines, or component status are reflected in the lifecycle strategy.
Five steps towards more resilient lifecycle planning
1. Identify critical components. Create a critical-parts matrix and record why each device is important, including the potential impact of replacement or redesign.
2. Define the program lifetime. Record expected production volumes, service-life requirements, and support horizons. A 10-year requirement may require a different approach from a 20-year requirement.
3. Capture compatibility parameters. For devices such as memory, document the characteristics that determine interchangeability, including speed, width, temperature, package, and die configuration.
4. Engage early. Establish dialogue with relevant semiconductor and lifecycle specialists before an EOL notice is received. Early visibility provides more time to assess available options.
5. Keep the information current. Program forecasts, design changes, and supply-chain developments can all affect lifecycle planning. Regular reviews help keep the strategy aligned with the product’s actual requirements.
Designing for longevity
Semiconductor obsolescence is a normal part of the technology lifecycle. Disruption does not have to be.
For long-life products, lifecycle thinking means considering not only whether a component meets today’s requirements, but also what may happen to it over the system’s expected life. Understanding criticality, documenting compatibility requirements, and maintaining an open dialogue around supply can all help reduce the disruption associated with future changes.
The result is not necessarily a way to eliminate obsolescence. Instead, it is a more structured approach to managing it, giving engineering teams greater visibility of potential risks and more time to consider their options.

articles.title: Stellantis reprend des couleurs, mais la convalescence s'annonce longue
articles.text:
Quand on a longtemps prétendu faire la course en tête avec une insolente rentabilité à deux chiffres, le réveil en salle de réanimation est brutal. Le mur contre lequel s’est fracassé le groupe Stellantis fin 2024, précipitant le départ de Carlos Tavares, a laissé des traces : une gueule de bois managériale et une remise à plat industrielle douloureuse, tant les plaies se sont avérées profondes.
Deux ans plus tard, le nouveau patron Antonio Filosa s’efforce de rassurer les marchés en répétant que le nouveau traitement fait effet. La volonté y est, on l’a sentie lors de la présentation des résultats du troisième trimestre, le 28 octobre. Mais siles signes vitaux s’améliorent, le patient européen repose sur des jambes flageolantes. La tête veut bien avancer, mais le corps peine à suivre le tempo imposé par la transition électrique.
L’illusion des volumes
À la lecture des derniers chiffres, la tentation de l’autosatisfaction est forte. En Europe, les livraisons grimpent de 10 % et les ventes de voitures électriques bondissent carrément de 65 %. Stellantis bombe le torse et se réjouit de l’engouement pour ses modèles issus de la plateforme « Smart Car », Citroën ë-C3 en tête. C’est le verre à moitié plein.
Sous le pansement, les comptes européensrestent dans le rouge : la marge opérationnelle ajustée plonge à -2,2 %, contre +1,2 % un an plus tôt. Les rabais consentis pour écouler la production pèsent sur les résultats. Et derrière le maquillage des nouveautés à succès, la réalité est moins glamour : lancements repoussés, bugs logiciels à répétition et perception de qualité en berne pour ces véhicules économiques.
C’est tout le paradoxe de Stellantis : le groupe parvient à surfer sur la vague de l’électrique abordable, mais avec un niveau de finition et de maturité technologique qui le pénalise lourdement. Imaginez un instant si Stellantis était capable d’aligner des propositions aussi abouties que certaines nouveautés de Volkswagen ou Renault… La satisfaction des résultats financiers n’aurait alors pas à être simulée.
Dans le creux de la vague des nouveautés
Le diagnostic le plus préoccupant se trouve peut-être dans le calendrier des lancements européens, qui ressemble davantage à un état léthargique qu’à la reprise espérée d’un groupe avec 14 marques. Sur les moquettes du Mondial de Paris, le groupe a pourtant su rallumer la flamme et nous faire rêver avec une belle brochette de concepts séduisants. Mais une fois l’enthousiasme des projecteurs retombé, le principe de réalité reprend ses droits : que restera-t-il concrètement de ces promesses stylistiques dans les concessions ?
Pour soigner la rentabilité et les volumes, Antonio Filosa mise beaucoup sur la future plateforme STLA One et la démocratisation massive de la chimie LFP à l’horizon 2027-2028. En attendant cette terre promise, que propose le groupe pour entretenir le pouls commercial ? Ce n’est pas avec le lancement de la Lancia Gamma que Stellantis va réanimer la flamme. Le futur Fiat Grizzly, cousin des Citroën ë-C3 Aircross et Opel Frontera, pourra certes attirer des curieux en concession. Mais le régime pain sec et eau ne tombe pas au meilleur moment.
Pendant ce temps, les machines à faire du volume vieillissent et leur relève se fait attendre. Dans un marché où la concurrence renouvelle ses armes à une vitesse inédite, Stellantis semble attendre sa plateforme miracle « à tout faire », les bras ballants.
La béquille Leapmotor
Pour donner le change, Stellantis a sorti sa béquille magique : Leapmotor. En intégrant les modèles chinois qu’il distribue en Europe, le groupe peut afficher une croissance électrique de 93 %, contre 65 % sans eux. De quoi faire bonne figure dans les présentations de résultats. Le soutien est précieux, mais son effet est à double tranchant. À trop s’appuyer sur sa marque chinoise pour gonfler ses statistiques, Stellantis ne risque-t-il pas d’anesthésier la compétitivité de ses propres marques historiques ? La question mérite d’être posée, même si Leapmotor peut aussi contribuer à élargir l’offre électrique du groupe et à attirer de nouveaux clients.
Le malade n’est pas condamné, loin de là : ne me faites pas dire le contraire. L’étincelle créative vue au Mondial de Paris prouve que l’ADN et la passion n’ont pas disparu sous les coupes budgétaires. La rationalisation reste titanesque, mais les changements de management semblent produire leurs premiers effets et le groupe maintient ses objectifs financiers. En Europe, toutefois, la convalescence sera longue.
Pour espérer une rémission complète, il faudra que les usines tournent rond, que les batteries suivent la cadence et, surtout, que le groupe retrouve la recette de ces voitures bien nées qui ont fait la gloire de ses marques. La guérison est en vue, mais le patient va devoir serrer les dents encore un moment.
