articles.title: 11.11 et Black Friday : les 25 meilleures offres tech du week-end chez AliExpress, Boulanger et Amazon
articles.text:
Ce dimanche 1er novembre, AliExpress déclenche son 11.11 avec des codes qui retranchent jusqu’à 120 €, au moment où Boulanger déroule déjà son Black Friday jusqu’au 30 novembre et où Amazon place ses premières offres à durée limitée. Nous avons gardé 25 offres tech, de la console au PC gamer, en vérifiant chaque prix sur la fiche du marchand.
Trois opérations se croisent ce week-end. Sur AliExpress, la remise du 11.11 passe par un code à saisir au moment de payer : le prix indiqué ici est celui obtenu une fois le code appliqué, le prix barré celui de la fiche avant le code. Chez Boulanger, le prix barré est le prix de référence affiché par l’enseigne. Chez Amazon, le Lenovo LOQ 15 et le Roborock Qrevo S Pro sont des offres à durée limitée, qui s’arrêtent les 13 et 12 novembre.
Un prix barré ne dit pas grand-chose de la vraie baisse. Sur AliExpress, nous avons donc comparé chaque prix avec celui affiché sur la même fiche le 30 octobre : avec le code, l’écart va de 13 % à 39 %. Les dix offres AliExpress sont expédiées depuis la France, mais sept passent par des revendeurs plutôt que par la boutique de la marque.
11.11 AliExpress et Black Friday : les 25 offres de notre sélection
- Nintendo Switch 2 à 367,87 € au lieu de 427,87 € avec le code 11FR60
- Pack Xiaomi 17T Pro + Redmi Buds 8 + Smart Band 11 Active à 749,99 € au lieu de 1 089,99 €
- Xiaomi 15T Pro à 439,46 € au lieu de 539,46 € avec le code FRD11100
- PC portable gamer Lenovo LOQ 15 (Ryzen 5 150, RTX 5060) à 1 099,99 € au lieu de 1 299,99 €
- Aspirateur balai Dyson V15 Detect Absolute à 549 € au lieu de 799 €
- Montre GPS Garmin Forerunner 255 à 125,28 € au lieu de 149,28 € avec le code 11FR24
- TV Mini LED TCL 55C89L 55 pouces (2026) à 799 € au lieu de 1 099 €
- Robot aspirateur laveur Roborock Qrevo S Pro à 379,99 € au lieu de 589,99 €
- Processeur AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D à 289,34 € au lieu de 349,34 € avec le code 11FR60
- PC portable Samsung Galaxy Book6 14 pouces à 599,99 € au lieu de 899,99 €
- Casque Bose QuietComfort Ultra à 299,99 € au lieu de 399,99 €
- Caméra 360 Insta360 X5 à 289,08 € au lieu de 349,08 € avec le code 11FR60
- Samsung Galaxy S25 FE à 397,65 € au lieu de 457,65 € avec le code 11FR60
- Écouteurs Samsung Galaxy Buds4 Pro à 160 € au lieu de 249,99 €
- PC portable Acer Swift Air 14 pouces à 599,99 € au lieu de 899,99 €
- Tablette Xiaomi Pad 7 à 202,35 € au lieu de 242,35 € avec le code 11FR40
- Enceinte JBL Charge 5 à 99,99 € au lieu de 199,99 €
- Drone DJI Mini 5 Pro à 499,05 € au lieu de 619,05 € avec le code FRD11120
- Barre de son Bose Smart Soundbar à 329 € au lieu de 549 €
- Robot aspirateur laveur Dreame L50 Ultra CE à 449 € au lieu de 599 €
- Écran PC gamer Asus ROG XG27AQWMG 27 pouces OLED à 469 € au lieu de 599,99 €
- Mini PC Chuwi AuBox Ryzen 7 8745HS (barebone) à 189,39 € au lieu de 229,39 € avec le code 11FR40
- Routeur Wi-Fi 7 TP-Link Deco BE22 (pack de 2) à 99,99 € au lieu de 199,99 €
- Nettoyeur vapeur Tineco Floor One S7 Steam à 177,48 € au lieu de 201,48 € avec le code 11FR24
- Station de recharge Belkin BoostCharge 3-en-1 Qi2 à 48,99 € au lieu de 129,99 €
VPN, logiciels, abonnements : les promos à saisir en ce moment
Six offres que nous avons regardées de près
Une remise ne pèse pas pareil sur une console, un PC portable ou un aspirateur. La Switch 2 ouvre la liste, et notre test de la Switch 2 en détaille les forces comme les limites ; pour les cinq autres, nous précisons à qui elles s’adressent et ce qui peut les rendre moins intéressantes.
- Nintendo Switch 2 : lancée à 469,99 €, la console descend à 367,87 € avec le code 11FR60. Nous avions salué son écran LCD de 7,9 pouces à 120 Hz, ses 256 Go de stockage et sa rétrocompatibilité avec les jeux Switch, en regrettant une autonomie en retrait, autour de 3 heures sur Tears of the Kingdom. Elle est vendue par un revendeur, Core Tech Store, et expédiée depuis la France.
- Pack Xiaomi 17T Pro : le smartphone arrive avec des écouteurs Redmi Buds 8, un bracelet Smart Band 11 Active et une coque, pour 250 € de moins que le prix de lancement du téléphone seul, 999,99 €. Batterie de 7 000 mAh, charge à 100 W et téléobjectif Leica 5x de 50 Mpx sont ses atouts ; son ultra grand-angle de 12 Mpx reste en retrait et le chargeur n’est pas fourni. Le pack parle surtout à ceux qui n’ont ni écouteurs sans fil ni bracelet d’activité.
- Lenovo LOQ 15 : avec sa RTX 5060, son Ryzen 5 150, 16 Go de mémoire et un écran Full HD à 144 Hz, ce PC portable vise le jeu en 1080p. Amazon le facture 200 € sous son plus bas prix des 30 derniers jours, en offre à durée limitée jusqu’au 13 novembre. Son clavier n’est pas rétroéclairé et la puissance de sa carte graphique n’est pas précisée.
- Dyson V15 Detect Absolute : noté 8/10 dans notre test, il combine une aspiration puissante, une filtration efficace et une brosse laser qui fait apparaître la poussière fine. Il pèse 3,1 kg en mode balai, ce qui se sent sur les longues séances, et le mode Boost vide vite la batterie. Boulanger le passe à 549 €, contre un prix de référence de 799 €.
- AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D : noté 9/10 dans notre test, c’est le processeur que nous recommandons pour jouer, avec 8 cœurs, 16 threads et 96 Mo de cache L3. À 289,34 € avec le code 11FR60, il arrive sans ventirad et réclame une carte mère AM5 : pour une configuration à monter de zéro, l’économie se dilue vite.
- Garmin Forerunner 255 : lancée à 349,99 €, la montre de course passe à 125,28 € avec le code 11FR24. Elle tient jusqu’à 14 jours en mode montre et 30 heures en GPS seul, avec un GPS multibande pour les parcours en ville ou en forêt. Son écran MIP manque de contraste en intérieur et cette version ne stocke pas de musique.
Ce que valent les remises de ce week-end
Les pourcentages affichés ne racontent pas la même chose d’un marchand à l’autre. Chez Boulanger, les -50 % de l’enceinte JBL Charge 5 et du routeur TP-Link Deco BE22 se mesurent au prix de référence de l’enseigne. Chez Amazon, le Lenovo LOQ 15 est comparé à son plus bas prix des 30 derniers jours, mais les autres offres le sont au prix conseillé, plus flatteur : c’est sur cette base que le chargeur Belkin affiche -62 %. Sur AliExpress, le code retranche de 24 à 120 €, et les codes FRD du Xiaomi 15T Pro et du DJI Mini 5 Pro s’arrêtent le 12 novembre, une semaine avant les autres.
Si la Switch 2 vous tente mais que vous hésitez encore, notre comparatif des meilleures consoles portables la situe face au Steam Deck OLED ou à l’ASUS ROG Ally, plus orientés PC. Pour les achats sur AliExpress, la mention « Expédié depuis » et le nom de la boutique figurent sur chaque fiche : mieux vaut les contrôler avant de valider le code.
Vos questions sur le 11.11 et le Black Friday
Comment utiliser un code promo du 11.11 sur AliExpress ?
Le code se saisit sur la page de paiement, avant de valider la commande. Chaque offre AliExpress de cette sélection indique le sien, et le prix affiché est celui obtenu une fois le code appliqué.
Jusqu’à quand durent ces offres ?
Les codes AliExpress 11FR24, 11FR40 et 11FR60 restent valables jusqu’au 18 novembre 2026, les codes FRD11100 et FRD11120 jusqu’au 12 novembre. L’opération Black Friday de Boulanger court jusqu’au 30 novembre, mais ses prix peuvent évoluer d’ici là, et les offres Amazon du Lenovo LOQ 15 et du Roborock Qrevo S Pro s’arrêtent les 13 et 12 novembre.
Les produits AliExpress sont-ils expédiés depuis l’Europe ?
Le 30 octobre, les dix fiches AliExpress retenues indiquaient une expédition depuis la France, donc sans frais d’importation. La mention peut changer selon la variante : elle se vérifie sur la fiche au moment de commander.
Comment profiter des offres exclusives du Black Friday ?
Durant tout le mois de novembre, Clubic vous propose chaque jour des sélections thématiques regroupant les meilleures offres à saisir en direct.
Retrouvez tous les bons plans du Black Friday 2026 sur la page dédiée à l'événement.
Pour les aficionados de X, n'hésitez pas à suivre notre compte Clubic Bons Plans pour être au courant en direct des meilleures offres.

articles.title: College student unofficially breaks world record for fastest jet-powered drone with 491 mph aircraft built in his dorm — Reaper aims to grab the $800,000 Boom Prize
articles.text:
College student unofficially breaks world record for fastest jet-powered drone with 491 mph aircraft built in his dorm — Reaper aims to grab the $800,000 Boom Prize
More jet-powered RC aircraft projects are aiming to reach Mach 1.
A new 'Reaper' jet-powered drone project just unofficially broke the previous drone speed world record of 465 mph by hitting 491 mph. Tomas Salvo is an aerospace engineering student at Georgia Tech, and his project was assembled in his dorm room. The drone is comprised of a custom-molded carbon fiber shell, laser-cut internal structure, and a 250N jet engine with a titanium 3D-printed nozzle, costing $13,000 to build. Tomas Salvo aims to win the $800,000 Boom Prize posted by Boom Supersonic CEO Blake Scholl.
Tomas Salvo’s Reaper project, which aimed to beat Niels Herbrich’s world record for the fastest jet-powered RC aircraft, went viral and caught the attention of Boom Supersonic CEO Blake Scholl, who sponsors the $800,000 Boom Prize ($750,000 cash, $50,000 Boom stock). The prize’s conditions are: First, pass Mach 1 for at least 5 seconds while climbing or level, not descending. Second, it must be an air-breathing aircraft with no on-board oxidizers or rockets for propulsion. Third, it must land intact, and lastly, the same aircraft (wings, fuselage, engine, and flight computer) must fly twice in one day. The participants must be individuals or teams, not corporations or people backed by venture capitalists or government funding; they want garage hobbyists.
We recently covered Mach Initiative’s Kingchaser, a 3D-printed jet-powered RC aircraft also aimed at beating Herbrich’s world record. They were beaten by Tomas Salvo, but Tomas’ run was not officially recorded by Guinness. The Kingchaser project was inspired by the Boom Prize; however, since they are not US citizens, they are not eligible to win it, but are still aiming to have an officially recorded Guinness World Record. The Reaper has a smaller engine than the Kingchaser at only 250N, compared to the Kingchaser’s 300N, but achieved a flight speed of 491 mph, beating the Kingchaser’s test flight of only 273 mph, as the latter did not have enough space to accelerate. However, Mach Initiative estimates a top speed of 550 mph if they had the space.
While the Reaper isn’t made out of PETG like the Kingchaser, it still utilizes some 3D printing, albeit in a much more expensive fashion — it has a titanium 3D-printed nozzle for its engine that replaces the stock nozzle, allowing the engine to sit further forward, improving the center of gravity without adding ballast on the front, weighing in at a total of 11 pounds. It’s made out of custom-molded carbon fiber on the outside with a laser-cut internal structure, all designed by Tomas Salvo and assembled in his dorm.
The Reaper was able to achieve its 491 mph speed while carrying a 1.2kg payload, with Tomas’ post further explaining that it could hold the speed for four minutes on a full tank, climb to 6,500 feet in under 20 seconds, and fly for a distance of 31 miles at full speed.
Before the Boom Prize, Tomas was able to land a few sponsorships that got him a JetCat 250N engine; however, we’re not sure how this fits with the Boom Prize’s rules barring corporate sponsorship. Since the Boom Prize's announcement, however, Tomas has resorted to crowdfunding, asking for $50,000 in August after raising $20,000, the source of which he did not disclose.
Both the Kingchaser and the Reaper are aiming at Herbrich’s world record, but they are still far from the 1,234.8 km/h or 767.3 mph Mach 1 speed that they need to surpass in order to win the Boom Prize. Mach Initiative responded to Blake Scholl’s X post about the Boom Prize, saying “challenge accepted,” but the rules may make them ineligible for the prize, making the Reaper a real contender for the $800,000, as it currently sits unrivaled by any other US project.

- me-three This matters more than meets the eye. UAV (aerial drone) combat is moving into the jet age. There's especially a great demand for cheap jet interceptors against jet-powered drones that are wreaking havoc in Ukraine, and soon to do the same in the Iran/ME war.
It's not just for govts, but also gangs and syndicates who are getting into the UAV action. Extrapolating the obvious, soon police forces will have it as well, more than just for surveillance, but for actual enforcement. Reply

articles.title: How voice AI is transforming banking and insurance: Desible.ai founders on the business behind the technology
articles.text:
How voice AI is transforming banking and insurance: Desible.ai founders on the business behind the technology
In this episode of the Prime Venture Partners Podcast, Gaurav Ranjan sits down with Uttam and Omkar to discuss what it takes to build and sell agentic AI in Indian BFSI, from product engineering and compliance to enterprise sales and scaling beyond the first use case.
From Rs 7 per minute to under Rs 2, voice AI is rapidly becoming cheaper. But Desible.ai co-founders Uttam Tiwari and Omkar Raikar believe the real opportunity lies beyond conversations, in automating the workflows that run large enterprises.
Building a voice AI agent that sounds human is no longer the hardest part of the problem. Getting that agent to operate reliably inside a bank or insurance company, navigate regulatory requirements, integrate with legacy systems and deliver measurable business outcomes is an entirely different challenge.
For Uttam Tiwari and Omkar Raikar, co-founders of Desible.ai, this distinction is shaping how they build their company. Desible is developing an agentic workflow orchestration platform for regulated enterprises, with an initial focus on insurance.
Speaking with Gaurav Ranjan, Principal at Prime Venture Partners, on the Prime Venture Partners Podcast, the founders discussed why AI pilots frequently fail to reach production, how enterprise buying behaviour is changing and why the economics of voice AI could fundamentally reshape the contact centre industry.
From 25 people to three: The moment that changed everything
Uttam and Omkar have known each other for 17 years. Their previous venture, Business Toys, was acquired in 2023, following which they worked with US enterprises, including Newsweek, Bank of America and Nestlé, through a software consulting and AI business.
The turning point came during a logistics brokerage project involving AI-powered calls to truckers for availability checks and verification. Following the implementation, the client restructured a contact centre of approximately 20 to 25 people to just three.
The experience demonstrated the potential of voice AI to change how enterprises operated. But as the founders explored the Indian market through proof-of-concept projects with 12 to 13 enterprises, they realised that automating conversations alone would not create a sufficiently differentiated business.
"Voice is a commodity. I do agree, but at the same time, workflows are not because workflow goes and sit deep inside organizational processes and that's where you get the moat," Uttam explained.
That insight led Desible to focus on insurance, where customer conversations are closely connected to renewals, persistency, claims, sales and servicing workflows.
Why AI demos succeed but production deployments fail
One of the most revealing discussions centred on the difference between demonstrating AI capabilities and deploying them inside regulated enterprises.
Uttam estimates that the conversion of proofs of concept into production deployments across the companies he has observed is below 35–40%. A successful demonstration, he argued, is only the beginning of a much more complicated journey.
Insurance companies require vendors to satisfy business teams, technology departments, information security teams, compliance functions and senior technology leadership before allowing systems into production.
Omkar described Indian information security reviews involving approximately 450 questions, including requirements around data residency and compute infrastructure. Even established international technology providers can struggle with these requirements.
Desible consequently invested much of its initial funding into building compliant infrastructure rather than concentrating exclusively on voice capabilities.
For Omkar, consistency is particularly important because insurance conversations leave little room for improvisation.
"You need to be speaking the same boring language every single time, staying compliant."
The technical challenges extend beyond compliance. Voice agents must manage interruptions, understand multilingual conversations, retrieve information from enterprise systems and respond appropriately without losing context.
In one example, Omkar explained how an AI agent conducting a medical questionnaire must recognise when a customer interrupts before hearing the complete question. In another, the system must identify a medicine mentioned during a conversation, verify it against a database and ask the appropriate follow-up question.
These capabilities distinguish a production-ready system from a conversational demonstration.
The economics of Voice AI are changing rapidly
The pricing of voice AI has undergone a dramatic shift. As Gaurav highlighted during the discussion, traditional human contact centre operations can cost approximately ₹20–₹30 per minute, while early voice AI solutions were priced at Rs 5–Rs 7 per minute.
Competitive pricing has since fallen to approximately Rs 1.5–Rs 3 per minute.
For startups building voice AI products, this creates an uncomfortable question: if the underlying technology keeps becoming cheaper, how can they capture a meaningful share of the value they create?
Omkar argued that per-minute pricing was never the natural economic model for contact centres, which historically charged based on seats or headcount. The emergence of voice AI introduced a pricing structure based on infrastructure and API consumption.
Desible is attempting to move beyond this model by charging for workflow execution rather than treating each call as an isolated transaction.
The company is already handling close to a million calls daily, according to Omkar. He also described how Desible has reduced its underlying call execution costs from approximately Rs 7–Rs 8 using earlier approaches to below Rs 1.5–Rs 2 through its orchestration capabilities.
However, the founders acknowledge that enterprise customers are still evaluating whether AI delivers sustainable returns.
Uttam shared an example of a customer that did not renew three small regional contact centres after Desible's solution had been running for approximately four and a half months.
The broader transition, he cautioned, remains gradual because enterprises need sustained operational evidence before reallocating budgets.
Enterprise buyers no longer care only about human-like voices
A year earlier, enterprise customers primarily evaluated voice AI through parameters such as latency, tone, language switching and how naturally an agent sounded.
That evaluation has changed. Today, Uttam explained, customers increasingly compare AI systems directly with human employees on contactability, conversion rates, lead qualification and the accuracy of information recorded after conversations.
The shift from technological novelty to measurable operational performance is also changing how Desible approaches enterprise sales.
Rather than pursuing every potential AI experiment, the company prioritises workflows that already exist within an organisation. Such processes have established owners, operating procedures, budgets and performance benchmarks, making it easier to demonstrate the value of automation.
"Your champion may not be your buyer," Uttam cautioned.
A business leader enthusiastic about an AI pilot may still lack the authority to approve deployment. Information security, technology, compliance and procurement teams can all influence the final decision.
For founders selling enterprise AI, identifying these stakeholders early can be as important as building the product itself.
In India, enterprise sales is as much about navigation as technology
Perhaps the most striking observation came when Gaurav asked whether enterprise sales was 40% product and 60% navigating internal organisational dynamics.
Omkar suggested that in India, the latter could account for as much as 80%.
Even a technically superior product, he argued, may fail without the ability to understand decision-making structures, secure internal support and sustain relationships across multiple stakeholders.
Desible's expansion strategy illustrates the approach. At one insurance customer, the company began with sales funnel management before expanding into welcome calls, persistency and inbound customer servicing.
Each successful workflow creates additional trust and reduces the effort required for subsequent integrations. Within insurance renewals alone, the company has identified more than 20 distinct workflows.
The founders believe that this combination of industry specialisation, compliance readiness and integration into existing enterprise processes creates a more durable advantage than voice quality alone.
Beyond voice: Building an operating system for insurance
Despite the competitive intensity surrounding voice AI, Omkar believes the market remains underexplored, particularly in India, where multiple languages, dialects, background noise and frequent language switching make conversational systems considerably more challenging.
He believes companies that solve these problems at scale could emerge as global leaders.
For Desible, however, the long-term ambition extends beyond handling calls. The founders envision an orchestration platform that supports insurance companies and intermediaries, including third-party administrators, brokers and health aggregators, across their operational workflows.
The ultimate measure of success will not be how convincingly an AI agent speaks, but whether it helps enterprises make better decisions, improve customer outcomes and operate more efficiently.
Uttam's assessment of where the industry currently stands captures the central lesson for AI founders:
"POC is overhyped but production is underhyped."
As enterprises move from experimenting with AI to demanding measurable results, the winners may not be the companies with the most impressive demonstrations, but those capable of turning AI into dependable infrastructure for everyday business operations.

articles.title: African creators need financial infrastructure
articles.text:
African creators have the talent and the audience. What holds them back is the infrastructure that turns attention into income. That was the thread through “Can African players build the infrastructure creators need?”, a panel at Moonshot by TechCabal on Thursday.
The session featured Richard Oyome, co-founder and COO of Raenest; Kene Okwuosa, founder and group CEO of Filmhouse Group; Darey Art Alade, co-founder and chief creative officer of Livespot360; and Kopano Cowen, CEO of Connect Channel. Kehinde Odusote-Fagbule of TechCabal Insights moderated.
The Nigerian Creator Economy Report 2025, found that 56.45% of Nigerian creators earn less than $100 a month from their work, while 3.23% earn more than $5,000. Money does reach some creators: Nigerian artists received more than ₦58 billion from Spotify in 2024, up 146% on 2023, according to the same report.
Platform payouts are part of the problem, as brand deals were often creators’ only route to income, because major platforms did not pay Nigerian creators directly until Meta switched on ads on Reels for creators in Nigeria and Ghana in 2024.
“We need to make the market bigger,” Oyome said, adding that the fix starts with growth. “We could penetrate foreign markets, especially in film, through collaboration, to produce better quality and attract international audiences.”
Getting paid from abroad is another barrier. Raenest, which offers dollar, pound and euro accounts to freelancers and creators, raised an $11 million Series A in February 2025 and said it had processed more than $1 billion in payments for over 700,000 individual customers.
Okwuosa rejected the idea that Nigeria’s market is small. “I don’t subscribe to the notion that the Nigerian market is small,” he said. “It only feels that way because we haven’t activated its size.” The real brake, he said, is piracy: “It limits the rewards and reach for creators.”
Estimates of what piracy costs Nollywood vary widely, which itself shows how little is measured. MultiChoice has put Nollywood’s annual losses at ₦10 billion to ₦15 billion, based on audience data, while other industry figures run far higher. TechCabal’s 2026 outlook adds that Netflix and Amazon Prime have cut African content spending, pushing more Nollywood filmmakers onto YouTube.
“Public-private partnerships can help expand the market,” Alade said. “We need policy and legislation that make it easier for these collaborations to happen.” The government has begun to move: its Creative Economy Development Fund is backed by a $200 million seed commitment from Afreximbank, according to the ministry.
The panellists agreed that the next wave of investment in the creator economy need not be a new standalone product. It could be a partnership or an acquisition that links players already working on payments, production, distribution and policy. For African builders, the opportunity lies in connecting what already exists.

articles.title: File Mover Express: AWS Releases Open-Source Tool for S3 File Transfers
articles.text:
AWS has recently released File Mover Express, an open-source application under the Apache 2.0 license for transferring large files between local systems and Amazon S3. Available for macOS, Windows, and Linux, it supports parallel transfers, automatic performance tuning, retries, pause and resume, and file integrity verification.
Designed to "move media to S3 at wire speed," File Mover Express supports auto-tuned parallel transfers, pause and resume, a desktop GUI, a scriptable CLI, and automatic uploads from monitored folders.
The project is primarily developed in Go for its transfer engine and TypeScript with Angular for its graphical interface. It also supports integration with AI assistants through MCP and OIDC-based authentication with identity providers. Provanshu Dey, senior solutions architect at AWS, Asbjorn Kjaer, senior software engineer at AWS, Matthew Muccio, solutions architect at AWS, and Ross Dickson, senior customer solutions manager at AWS, explain:
At the core of File Mover Express is a daemon-based transfer engine that decouples transfers from your desktop session. The daemon can run on the machine of your choice, whether that is your workstation, a server in the data center, or an Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance, while you control it from a drag-and-drop graphical user interface (GUI) or a scriptable command line interface (CLI) over an encrypted, password-protected connection.
Media teams regularly transfer terabytes of assets between on-premises storage and the cloud. These transfers often involve tight deadlines and processes that must continue after the initiating user or machine disconnects. Traditional transfer clients may stop when a desktop session ends, while commercial alternatives can introduce licensing costs, proprietary protocols, or third-party infrastructure. File Mover Express supports uploads and downloads, allowing teams to transfer large files to Amazon S3 and retrieve them for editing, review, or restoration.
Source: GitHub project
File Mover Express splits large files into chunks and uploads them in parallel using multipart uploads. With the autotuning mode, it adjusts the number of parallel streams and chunk sizes to optimize throughput for the available connection. Transfers also support configurable retries and file-level pause and resume. Dey, Kjaer, Muccio, and Dickson add:
File Mover Express provides security features including file encryption in flight, file encryption at rest, and encryption for the control plane. All transfers use HTTPS, and access to your S3 buckets is governed by AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) with a documented minimum-permission policy (...) For teams that centralize identity, File Mover Express supports single sign-on through OpenID Connect (OIDC).
File Mover Express calculates checksums in the background and caches them locally for reuse when files remain unchanged. It supports MD5, XXHash, XXHash64, and XXH3, offering a choice between compatibility and hashing performance. For transfers to distant buckets, users can enable S3 Transfer Acceleration, while bandwidth limits help control network usage. On LinkedIn, Dickson writes:
Moving large media files to the cloud shouldn't be the slow part of your day :) That’s why a group of us at AWS built File Mover Express (...) For anyone in media moving camera cards, dailies, or deliverables, it tackles the usual pain.
The project's source code is available on GitHub, along with pre-built packages for macOS, Windows, and Linux.

articles.title: Intel's next budget laptop chip may have no performance cores at all
articles.text:
Rumor mill: Intel's next processor for low-cost Windows laptops and mini PCs is starting to come into focus, if a new leak is accurate. Hardware leaker Jaykihn has posted base specifications for the chip, code-named Moon Lake, describing a processor with four low-power efficiency cores and zero performance cores.
Intel's current entry-level N-series chips also skip performance cores, and Moon Lake would bring that approach to the company's newer tile-based design. If the leak holds, it would be the next generation of the N-series processors found in many budget machines. Intel has not confirmed the specs.
The leaked table lists a thermal design power (TDP) range of 6W to 15W. The low end sits close to the power envelope of phone and tablet system-on-chips. At 15W, laptop makers would have room to trade some efficiency for sustained performance when the cooling allows it.
The table also suggests Moon Lake will share its layout with Wildcat Lake, the Core Series 3 processor family Intel launched in April. Wildcat Lake pairs up to two performance cores with four LP-E cores, which sit in their own low-power island on the compute tile.
Moon Lake appears to drop the performance cores and keep the island. It reportedly retains the compute tile, the multi-tile design and Wildcat Lake's BGA1516 package, and the cores are said to be Darkmont LP-E designs, the same type used in Wildcat Lake's low-power island.
On paper, Moon Lake looks a lot like the chips it would replace. Entry-level N-series processors such as the N150, which power many ultra-budget machines, also pair four efficiency cores with a 6W TDP. The core count and power budget stay the same. What changes is the generation of the cores themselves.
 – Jaykihn (@jaykihn0) October 29, 2026
 – Jaykihn (@jaykihn0) October 28, 2026
That's where most of the gains are likely to come from. A newer architecture with higher instructions per clock (IPC) should make Moon Lake somewhat faster than its predecessors at the same core count. For buyers, the bigger change may be battery life: if the cores do more work per cycle within the same 6W budget, a system can finish a task sooner and fall back to idle sooner, which helps in thin, cheap designs.
Clock speeds are missing from the leak. For reference, the N150 reaches a 3.6GHz turbo. Intel's recent chips hint at what to expect: Panther Lake and Wildcat Lake, both built on the 18A process this year, broadly match the clock speeds of the chips they replaced. That suggests Moon Lake's gains would come from architecture rather than frequency.
N-series chips sit in the lowest tier of Windows laptops and mini PCs, where cost matters more than raw speed. Systems built on Moon Lake would likely land around $300 to $500, though that range is uncertain. RAM and storage prices have been pushed around by demand from AI data centers, and Moon Lake reportedly isn't expected until 2028, so NAND and DDR supply could shift a lot before then, changing what these machines cost.
The leak caps a busy year for Intel's client chips. Panther Lake arrived early in the year and Wildcat Lake followed in April, and Intel has said little about its consumer roadmap since. Some newer models in those families added cores. Moon Lake appears to move the other way, keeping the core count low and focusing on doing more within a very small power budget.
Many details are still unconfirmed, including clocks, graphics and memory support. The leak reportedly points to Intel's 18A node for the compute tile. Like any pre-announcement leak, the specs could change before launch, or Intel may never confirm them.

articles.title: AWS Capacity Largely Sold Out Through 2027, With On Demand Headroom Reserved
articles.text:
Amazon CEO Andy Jassy recently said that AWS’s large committed cloud capacity is largely sold out through 2027, with a good chunk of 2028 already allocated, while the company continues to reserve headroom for On Demand, EC2 and Bedrock.
Jassy made the remarks in a video podcast with Andreessen Horowitz co-founder Ben Horowitz and general partner Erik Torenberg, reported by Reuters on October 23. AWS sells capacity assurance through On-Demand Capacity Reservations and Capacity Blocks for ML, where a customer reserves instances in a named Availability Zone, and in the Capacity Blocks case, for a fixed window beginning on a future date. As previously reported on InfoQ, AWS raised Capacity Blocks for ML rates by about 15% uniformly across every region in January, covering P5en, P5e, P5 and P4d GPU instances along with Trn2 and Trn1.
Capacity for 2026 is already gone, Jassy said, and the company could invest well beyond the roughly $220 billion in capital expenditure planned for this year without it being a poor use of capital. On the allocation itself:
2027 is largely sold out. We always leave a certain amount for on demand and our inference service bedrock, or EC2, but largely sold out all the big chunks. A good chunk of 2028 is sold out.
Cloud analyst David Linthicum argued that the reporting overstated the position, drawing a distinction between the pre-reserved blocks Jassy described and what an enterprise can allocate day to day:
Of course, I suspect I can still go into the AWS console today and allocate GPU capacity for AI workloads. Maybe not the exact massive, pre-reserved, hyperscale capacity block some large model provider wants for the next three years, but that’s not exactly the same thing as "AWS is sold out."
Linthicum added that the market already carries enough confusion around reserved instances, on-demand services and committed capacity, and that headlines of this kind lead to bad assumptions and bad strategy.
Discussion on Reddit turned to current availability rather than the 2027 commitments. The highest-rated comment, from a developer posting as cbigsby, describes constraints on ordinary instance types:
We’ve been seen a big rise in compute capacity issues the past month or so at work, just for regular ec2 instances. Forget spot instances we have trouble getting enough on demand. Luckily mostly tied to CI but there have been a few days where the production k8s clusters have been concerningly constrained.
Similar reports appeared elsewhere. Richard T., a technical operations manager, commented on Linthicum’s post that Microsoft has released only limited information about Azure East US capacity constraints, and that his team adopted reserved instances to secure capacity against projected growth. A commenter in a parallel thread reported trouble obtaining sufficient compute from any of the three major providers, and said the constraint was not limited to GPUs.
Ian Rae, replying to Linthicum, pointed to the architectural consequence of that response:
next thing you know, folks reserve cloud resources they are worried they might need, which is an anti-cloud pattern
AWS already ships tooling for the problem Rae describes. As reported on InfoQ last October, EC2 Capacity Manager aggregates capacity data into a cross-account, cross-region dashboard and reports the ratio of used to unused reserved capacity as a measure of reservation efficiency.
The $220 billion figure covers total capital expenditure rather than AI spending alone, a distinction raised by commenters in both threads. Amazon reports third-quarter results on October 29, where its remaining performance obligations disclosure will show how much of the committed capacity is contracted revenue.

articles.title: Câncer de pulmão: comprimido diário mantém doença avançada controlada por 7 anos
articles.text:
Um comprimido tomado uma vez ao dia conseguiu manter o câncer de pulmão avançado sob controle por sete anos em mais da metade dos pacientes que participaram de um estudo clínico. O resultado, considerado inédito para a doença, foi obtido com o lorlatinibe, medicamento desenvolvido para combater tumores que apresentam alteração genética específica.
Publicado em setembro de 2026 na revista científica Annals of Oncology, o estudo é atualização de sete anos do ensaio clínico de fase 3 CROWN. Os resultados mostram que 55% dos pacientes tratados com lorlatinibe permaneceram vivos e sem progressão da doença após esse período.
O levantamento acompanhou 296 pessoas com câncer de pulmão de não pequenas células avançado e positivo para a alteração genética ALK. Desse total, 149 receberam lorlatinibe e 147 foram tratadas com crizotinibe, outro medicamento utilizado contra esse subtipo de tumor.
No grupo que recebeu o tratamento mais recente, a mediana de sobrevida livre de progressão ainda não havia sido alcançada após sete anos de acompanhamento. Já entre os pacientes tratados com crizotinibe, esse indicador foi de apenas 9,1 meses. A probabilidade de permanecer vivo e sem progressão da doença após sete anos foi de 3% nesse segundo grupo.
Os pesquisadores também calcularam redução de 81% no risco de progressão da doença ou morte entre os pacientes que receberam lorlatinibe, na comparação com o crizotinibe.
O resultado representa avanço importante no tratamento do câncer de pulmão avançado. Entretanto, o medicamento não funciona para todos os pacientes e ainda enfrenta obstáculos de acesso no Brasil.
Medicamento ataca alteração genética específica
- O lorlatinibe é um exemplo do que os oncologistas chamam de terapia-alvo: medicamentos desenvolvidos para combater alterações genéticas específicas que estimulam o crescimento de tumores;
- No caso do câncer de pulmão, uma dessas alterações envolve o gene ALK. Em aproximadamente 3% a 5% dos casos de câncer de pulmão de não pequenas células, ocorre um rearranjo nesse gene, que leva à produção de proteína anormal responsável por enviar sinais contínuos de crescimento e multiplicação às células;
- O lorlatinibe atua bloqueando essa proteína e interrompendo o mecanismo que favorece o desenvolvimento do tumor.
Uma das características importantes do medicamento é sua capacidade de atravessar a barreira hematoencefálica, estrutura que protege o cérebro e dificulta a entrada de diversas substâncias, inclusive alguns medicamentos.
Isso é relevante porque pacientes com câncer de pulmão avançado podem desenvolver metástases cerebrais. O lorlatinibe foi projetado para atuar também nesses casos, além de combater mecanismos de resistência que podem comprometer a eficácia de tratamentos anteriores.
Os resultados de sete anos reforçam esse potencial. No estudo CROWN, não foram registrados novos episódios de progressão intracraniana depois dos primeiros 30 meses de tratamento com lorlatinibe.
Entre os pacientes que chegaram ao fim dos dois primeiros anos sem progressão da doença, a probabilidade estimada de continuarem vivos e sem avanço do câncer no sétimo ano foi de 79%.
Resultado representa mudança histórica no tratamento
O avanço chama atenção quando comparado às alternativas disponíveis em gerações anteriores.
Durante décadas, a quimioterapia era uma das principais opções para tratar o câncer de pulmão avançado. Com o desenvolvimento dos inibidores de ALK, os médicos passaram a contar com medicamentos mais direcionados, capazes de prolongar o controle da doença.
Segundo o oncologista Gustavo Schvartsman, do Hospital Sírio-Libanês, a evolução pode ser observada nos resultados obtidos ao longo das diferentes gerações de medicamentos.
“Nunca alguém passava de cinco anos sem a doença progredir quando só existia quimioterapia. Com os inibidores de primeira geração, foi para 5% ou 10% dos pacientes; com a segunda geração, 20% a 30%; agora chegamos a 55%. O avanço é muito grande e vemos um passo enorme no dia a dia do paciente”, afirmou ao g1.
O oncologista Stephen Stefani também destacou a importância do acompanhamento prolongado para avaliar a eficácia do tratamento. “A diferença de eficácia se torna muito gritante quando você vê essa análise de sete anos e é um resultado relevante para o paciente”, avaliou.
Matheus Henrique Dias, biomédico e pesquisador de medicamentos contra o câncer na Holanda, também considera os resultados promissores. “Para quem tem essa mutação específica, vai ser de fato uma mudança grande”, afirmou.
Apesar do entusiasmo, há uma ressalva: os dados de sobrevida global ainda não estão maduros. Isso significa que o estudo ainda não acumulou o número de mortes necessário para realizar a análise definitiva desse indicador.
Portanto, os resultados demonstram um controle prolongado da doença, mas não permitem afirmar que o medicamento representa uma cura para o câncer de pulmão avançado.
Leia mais:
- China apresenta novo medicamento experimental para tratar câncer de pulmão
- Adenocarcinoma de pulmão: o que é a doença detectada no Papa Leão XIV
- Anvisa aprova novo remédio contra câncer de pulmão; Brasil é o 2º país a liberar terapia
Efeitos colaterais ainda preocupam especialistas
O desempenho do lorlatinibe também precisa ser analisado considerando os efeitos adversos.
Na atualização de sete anos do estudo CROWN, eventos adversos de grau 3 ou 4 foram registrados em 77% dos pacientes que receberam o medicamento. Na maioria dos casos, esses eventos não significam necessariamente que foram provocados diretamente pelo tratamento.
A análise também mostrou que 34% dos participantes precisaram reduzir a dose do medicamento em algum momento. Ainda assim, a eficácia de longo prazo foi semelhante entre pacientes que passaram por redução de dose e aqueles que não precisaram dessa alteração.
Outro aspecto importante envolve os efeitos no sistema nervoso central. Dados de segurança reunidos em diferentes estudos clínicos indicam que esse tipo de reação pode ocorrer em 52% dos pacientes que recebem lorlatinibe.
Entre as manifestações estão alterações cognitivas, mudanças de humor, problemas de fala, distúrbios do sono e, em alguns casos, sintomas psiquiátricos mais graves.
Na análise específica de cinco anos do estudo CROWN, efeitos no sistema nervoso central foram registrados em 42% dos participantes tratados com lorlatinibe. A maioria foi classificada como leve ou moderada.
Para Matheus Henrique Dias, o avanço científico precisa ser acompanhado de atenção à qualidade de vida dos pacientes. “A gente vê que ainda há alguns pontos que precisam ser considerados. É importante que as pessoas vivam, mas é muito importante que elas continuem sendo, em boa medida, elas mesmas”, afirmou.
Paciente brasileira recupera perspectiva de futuro
Uma das pessoas que vivem os efeitos do tratamento é Paula Piteri. Ela tinha 38 anos quando descobriu, em 2020, que um nódulo no pulmão era câncer. Na época, tinha acabado de se tornar mãe e levava vida saudável, sem histórico de tabagismo. A descoberta aconteceu durante um exame de rotina.
Inicialmente, Paula não realizou o sequenciamento genético do tumor. Ela passou por cirurgia para retirar a lesão e acreditou que estaria livre da doença. Entretanto, em 2025, recebeu um novo diagnóstico: o câncer havia voltado. “Foi um choque, eu sou mãe de três crianças e isso podia mudar minha vida completamente”, contou.
Atualmente, Paula utiliza lorlatinibe, fornecido pelo plano de saúde. O medicamento está previsto na cobertura da saúde suplementar para as indicações contempladas pelas regras da Agência Nacional de Saúde Suplementar (ANS).
“É muito bom ter perspectiva, saber que eu tenho vida para viver. Eu quero fazer parte disso e viver por muitos anos ainda”, afirmou.
Medicamento custa R$ 37 mil por mês e não está disponível no SUS
Apesar dos resultados promissores, o acesso ao lorlatinibe ainda é um desafio no Brasil.
Antes mesmo de iniciar o tratamento, o paciente precisa identificar se o tumor apresenta a alteração genética ALK. Isso exige exames moleculares que nem sempre estão disponíveis na rede pública ou são facilmente acessíveis por meio dos planos de saúde.
Para Gustavo Schvartsman, existe dificuldade em garantir que diagnóstico e tratamento caminhem juntos. “Não adianta fazer o teste num sistema em que o remédio não vai estar disponível. E não adianta ter o remédio se o paciente não conseguiu o diagnóstico correto”, resumiu.
O preço também representa um obstáculo. Segundo a tabela de preços de medicamentos, uma caixa com 30 comprimidos pode chegar a aproximadamente R$ 37 mil.
Considerando um tratamento contínuo durante sete anos, o custo ultrapassaria R$ 3,1 milhões por paciente, sem considerar eventuais reajustes ou descontos.
A incorporação do lorlatinibe ao Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) chegou a ser analisada pela Comissão Nacional de Incorporação de Tecnologias no SUS (Conitec). Em maio de 2025, porém, o Ministério da Saúde publicou decisão contrária à disponibilização do medicamento para pacientes com câncer de pulmão de não pequenas células com alteração ALK em estágio localmente avançado ou metastático, na primeira linha de tratamento.
A decisão também rejeitou a incorporação do alectinibe, enquanto aprovou o brigatinibe para essa indicação.
A justificativa da comissão envolveu a relação entre os custos e os benefícios clínicos das terapias avaliadas. Segundo o relatório, os valores apresentados não atingiram os critérios de custo-efetividade considerados adequados para o SUS.
Com isso, pacientes que precisam do lorlatinibe dependem de cobertura por planos de saúde, aquisição particular ou decisões judiciais para conseguir acesso ao tratamento pela rede pública.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: CVSS 10.0 LXD, MicroCloud Flaw Lets Attackers Impersonate Trusted Clients Without a Private Key
articles.text:
A critical flaw in Canonical's LXD and MicroCloud let an attacker log in as a trusted client without holding that client's private key. To do it, the attacker had to reach their HTTPS API over the network and have the trusted client's public certificate.
Once in, the attacker would act as that client, with access to the cluster and its virtual machines. If the impersonated account is privileged, the attacker could gain "root access to the host machine," Canonical said.
The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-112816, carries a maximum CVSS score of 10.0, and Canonical has released fixed versions of both products.
How the Flaw Works
LXD and MicroCloud let remote clients access their APIs over mutual TLS, a setup in which the client presents a certificate to prove who it is. A client is trusted when its certificate is in the server's trust store, the list of identities the server will accept.
The flaw was in how the server checked that certificate. It compared every certificate the client sent against the trust store, but a TLS connection only proves the client owns the private key for the first certificate in the chain, the leaf. The rest of the chain is whatever the client chose to attach.
So an attacker could take a trusted client's public certificate, which is not secret, attach it to the chain behind their own, and the server would accept them as that client.
Who Is Affected
Using the flaw takes two things: network access to the HTTPS API, and the public certificate of a client the server already trusts.
A standalone LXD server does not expose that API by default. It listens only on a local socket unless an administrator turns on the network API with the core.https_address setting.
MicroCloud, which ties several machines running LXD into one cluster, has a specific weak point. Canonical said an attacker who can capture a member's public certificate as it joins the cluster can then log in as that member.
The CVE record lists LXD 4.0.14, 5.0.10, 5.21.8 and 6.9 as affected, each before the fixed release that follows. Canonical lists these fixed snap versions:
| Product | Snap channel | Fixed version | 
|---|---|---|
| LXD | 6/stable | 6.10.1 | 
| LXD | 5.21/stable | 5.21.9 | 
| LXD | 5.0/stable | 5.0.11 | 
| LXD | 4.0/stable | 4.0.15 | 
| MicroCloud | 3/stable | 3.4.1 | 
| MicroCloud | 2/stable | 2.1.5 | 
The bug did not start at Canonical. The Incus project, which began as a community fork of LXD, reported it, and Canonical confirmed it affected LXD as well. Incus fixed the same flaw in version 7.6.0.
Ubuntu's own archive packages of LXD are listed as not affected or not shipped, so the fixed releases are the snaps.
There is no public sign the flaw has been used in an attack. The CVE record carries a U.S. CISA assessment, dated October 30, that the flaw is not known to have been exploited; it is not on CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list, and no working exploit has been published.
What to Do
Update LXD and MicroCloud to the fixed versions. On a snap install, run sudo snap refresh lxd and sudo snap refresh microcloud.
Canonical said the fixed LXD point releases were still rolling out from the candidate channel to stable at the time of its advisory, so check the version you actually have after the refresh rather than assume the fix arrived.
Canonical's advisory gives no temporary workaround for LXD. Because the attack requires network access to the API, limiting who can reach it reduces risk until you update. The Incus project, reporting the same flaw, said there is no configuration fix and that the only step is to restrict network access to the listener.
Incus users should move to 7.6.0, which fixed this flaw along with 17 other security issues.

articles.title: The solar system may have a sixth dwarf planet, hidden against the Milky Way
articles.text:
First look: The solar system's official roster of dwarf planets has held at five names since 2008. But a new observatory in Chile has spotted an icy world beyond Pluto that could become the sixth. It might also be the largest object found out past Neptune in about 20 years.
For now, the object announced by the Vera C. Rubin Observatory team earlier this week only goes by its provisional designation, 2026 ED138. It currently sits about 46 astronomical units from the Sun. Pluto, by comparison, averages around 40.
Nobody has measured its size directly yet. Instead, astronomers worked backward from how bright it looks at that distance, plus an estimate of how reflective its surface is, to arrive at somewhere between 600 and 1,500 km across. Even the middle of that range sits close to Ceres, the smallest dwarf planet on the official list. Rubin's solar system lead Mario Jurić put it at roughly 1,000 km and called it a once-in-a-generation kind of find.
It stayed hidden this long mostly because of where it sits in the sky. From Earth, ED138 lines up close to the plane of the Milky Way, where it's just one more faint dot against millions of background stars.
But Rubin photographs the whole southern sky every few nights with the largest digital camera ever built for astronomy, so the same dot keeps turning up in a slightly different spot. On October 13, Harvard & Smithsonian astrophysicist Matthew Holman ran data from earlier this year through a search code he wrote with colleague Kevin Napier.
ED138 caught his eye because it looked far too bright for something that far out. Holman admitted his first instinct was to check whether he or the code had messed up.
Jurić's search through Rubin's catalog put that doubt to rest – the object shows up in 30 images across 20 nights between March and July. Older survey images push its track all the way back to 2016, too.
None of that settles whether it's a dwarf planet, though. To earn the label, an object has to be massive enough for its own gravity to pull it round. Confirming that for ED138 will take infrared observations that can nail down its true size.
Even then, an official title could take a while. Quaoar and Gonggong are already treated as dwarf planets in plenty of research papers, yet the International Astronomical Union still hasn't added either one to its list. In the meantime, anyone curious can follow ED138's orbit in 3D on Orbitviewer.

articles.title: Cómo evitar las llamadas comerciales y el spam telefónico en tu Samsung Galaxy
articles.text:
Recibir una llamada telefónica se ha convertido en una pesadilla para muchas personas. Entre las llamadas comerciales y los intentos de phishing o estafas por teléfono, nadie está a salvo de ser molestado. A pesar de la lista Robinson y de la nueva normativa que obliga a emplear el prefijo 400 con fines promocionales, los timos se saltan estas normas. Así que la única solución que te queda es configurar tu teléfono móvil. Sin ir más lejos, puedes evitar el spam en tu Samsung Galaxy activando las herramientas oficiales que vienen instaladas por defecto.
Con anterioridad hemos hablado de los métodos que puedes utilizar para detectar llamadas fraudulentas, confirmar que tu banco te está llamando realmente o cómo configurar Android para bloquear llamadas de spam. En este sentido, Google lleva años incorporando nuevas herramientas para facilitar la detección de las llamadas no deseadas. Pero no siempre llegan a todos los teléfonos móviles con Android.
Y si tienes un Samsung Galaxy, que es una de las marcas más populares, las herramientas de Android se ven complementadas con las que el gigante coreano incorpora a One UI, su capa de personalización. Así, cada nueva versión de One UI añade más fórmulas para evitar spam y llamadas inoportunas. A continuación veremos las que te resultarán más útiles y efectivas.
Bloquear números desconocidos
Empezaremos por la opción más popular que sirve para evitar spam en Samsung Galaxy, pero también en otros móviles Android. Sin embargo, en esta ocasión, usaremos las opciones que ofrece Samsung en vez de las de Google. Su nombre es Bloquear números desconocidos, pero tal y como indica la ayuda oficial del fabricante, sirve para bloquear las llamadas con número oculto. Este tipo de llamada es muy molesta porque, al no haber un número de referencia, no puedes buscar en internet si se trata de una estafa o de un número oficial.
Para bloquear números desconocidos, sigue estos pasos:
- Abre la aplicación Teléfono de tu Samsung Galaxy.
- Pulsa el menú de tres puntos para entrar en Ajustes.
- Dentro de Ajustes de llamada, accede a Bloquear números.
- Activa la opción Bloquear números desconocidos.
- Opcionalmente, puedes añadir números concretos.
- Puedes añadir números que te han llamado antes pulsando en Recientes.
- O incorporar números que tengas guardados pulsando en Contactos.
Bloquear llamadas no deseadas y de estafas
Desde hace unos años, para evitar spam en Samsung Galaxy, los teléfonos de esta compañía incorporan una aplicación exclusiva llamada Smart Call. Su labor es, precisamente, “detectar y bloquear llamadas no deseadas”. Desarrollada junto a la empresa Hiya, tiene varias opciones que te resultarán muy útiles para combatir el phishing telefónico.
- Identificador de llamadas. Muy útil, especialmente, para empresas y negocios.
- Aviso de sospecha de spam. Además, facilita el bloqueo del número.
- Aviso de posible fraude. Junto a la opción de bloquear o denunciar ese número.
Para activar estas opciones de Smart Call de Samsung:
- Abre la aplicación Teléfono de tu Samsung Galaxy.
- Pulsa el menú de tres puntos para entrar en Ajustes.
- Dentro de Ajustes de llamada, activa la opción ID llamante y protección spam.
- En inglés, Caller ID and spam protection.
Dentro del menú de ID llamante y protección spam, hay otra opción interesante para bloquear las llamadas automáticamente a partir de la lista facilitada por Hiya. Actívala sólo si las opciones anteriores no te han servido. Te dará a elegir entre bloquear todas las llamadas registradas como no deseadas y de estafadores o bloquear solo las llamadas de estafadores registradas como alto riesgo.
Por otra parte, también puedes activar Samsung Smart Call desde el registro de llamadas y desde las notificaciones, siempre y cuando aparezca el mensaje indicando que estas opciones están disponibles en tu modelo de Samsung Galaxy.
Filtrado de llamadas para evitar spam en Samsung Galaxy
Las herramientas anteriores están disponibles en la mayoría de dispositivos Samsung Galaxy. Y si, además, tienes un modelo reciente como, por ejemplo, un Samsung Galaxy S26, podrás utilizar una herramienta para evitar el spam en Samsung Galaxy utilizando el asistente de IA. Esta función relativamente nueva se llama Filtrado de llamadas y “permite que el Asistente de llamadas responda llamadas y le pregunte a la persona que llama quién es y por qué llama. Verás en la pantalla lo que dice la persona que llama y la IA, aunque no respondas a la llamada. Aun así, puedes responder la llamada en cualquier momento o cambiar a Llamada de texto”.
Para activar el Filtrado de llamadas en tu Samsung Galaxy:
- Abre la aplicación Teléfono.
- Pulsa el menú de tres puntos para entrar en Ajustes.
- Dentro de Ajustes de llamada, entra en Filtrado de llamadas.
- Allí deberás elegir un idioma.
- A continuación, pulsa el interruptor para mostrar el mensaje Activado.
Por defecto, este filtrado es manual. Pero puedes hacerlo automático si pulsas en Filtrar llamadas automáticamente siguiendo los pasos anteriores. Te dará a elegir entre dos opciones:
- Sospechas de spam y estafas. “Números de teléfono en bases de datos públicas de spam y estafas. Incluye números privados”.
- Llamadas de origen desconocido. Afecta a números que no tengas guardados en tus contactos, que no estén etiquetados en tu historial de llamadas, que no sean de emergencia y que no hayan hablado contigo antes.
Para utilizar esta función y evitar spam en tu Samsung Galaxy con ayuda de la IA, cuando recibas una llamada pulsa la opción Asistente de llamadas y, a continuación, Filtrado de llamadas. Si ves que te interesa atender la llamada, simplemente toca el botón verde Descolgar o Llamada.

articles.title: Tokenization helps enterprises move AI agents into production - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Project-by-project security reviews can’t keep pace with enterprise AI agents
Enterprises racing to put AI agents into production are finding that tokenization and other data protection methods now decide how fast those projects move.
But sensitive data fed into models is hard to pull back — and security reviews built for a slower era are stalling deployments. The challenge is shifting from locking data down to keeping it usable once it is protected. That tension is playing out across Cloudera Inc.’s partner ecosystem, where security is becoming a prerequisite for AI value rather than a final gate, according to Diego Loureda (pictured), vice president of customer success and presales at Protegrity USA Inc.
“Data leaks are still a thing. If you put sensitive data on a model, if you put sensitive data on a vector store or in the memory of an agent that is going to propagate to other agents, good luck removing that sensitive data,” Loureda said. “There’s no way you’re going to be able to do that.”
Loureda spoke with theCUBE’s Rebecca Knight and Paul Gillin at Cloudera EVOLVE26, during an exclusive interview on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed data security along with Protegrity being named Cloudera’s Emerging Technology Partner of the Year. (* Disclosure below.)
Tokenization keeps protected data usable for AI
Traditional encryption can lock data so tightly that analysts and models can no longer use it. Protegrity centers its approach on tokenization, which swaps sensitive values for substitutes instead of relying on a mathematical algorithm, Loureda explained. That design also matters as quantum computing threatens today’s cryptography.
“Our main method of protection, that is tokenization, it’s already quantum ready,” Loureda said. “The reason behind that is because there is no mathematical algorithm behind it. It’s all based on replacement in memory.”
Protection alone doesn’t solve the speed problem, however. In research Protegrity commissioned from Enterprise Management Associates Inc., 83% of leaders reported project delays, Loureda noted.
“The main problem with governance is that companies are approving projects and that will not scale in the age of AI,” Loureda said. “They have to approve patterns.”
The same study found 82% of leaders push agents into production in a diminished state, stripped of the tools and data that would make them useful, he added. Controls such as tokenization let security teams clear the way for those agents instead, according to Loureda.
“Security has always been the business of no, the department of no. That changes now,” he said. “These days security is the team that can enable AI to give you value.”

articles.title: „Sinnlos geworden“: Dieser Mathe-Professor will die Hausaufgaben seiner Studenten nicht mehr bewerten
articles.text:
Mathe-Professor kapituliert: Warum KI-Hausaufgaben nicht mehr benotbar sind
KI hat die Art und Weise, wie junge Menschen studieren, grundlegend verändert und zwingt auch Professor:innen zum Umdenken. Richard Borcherds von der UC Berkeley sieht beispielsweise keinen Sinn mehr darin, die Hausaufgaben seiner Kursteilnehmer:innen zu benoten. Der Einsatz von KI sei unvermeidbar geworden. Es sei daher sinnlos, Lehrkräfte dafür zu bezahlen, die Hausarbeiten der Student:innen auf ihre Richtigkeit zu prüfen.
Wandel der universitären Lernkultur durch KI
Im vergangenen Jahr ergab eine OpenAI-Analyse, dass in den USA College-Student:innen ChatGPT häufiger nutzen als jede andere Zielgruppe. „Sie treffen keine wichtigen Lebensentscheidungen mehr, ohne vorher ChatGPT um Rat zu fragen, was sie tun sollen”, erklärte CEO Sam Altman Mitte 2025 auf einem Event. Viele setzen KI ein, um Zeit zu sparen. Einige Student:innen fügen sogar gezielt Tippfehler hinzu oder verwenden „dumme” Prompts, damit ihre Texte natürlicher klingen und nicht auffallen. In Deutschland ist KI im Studium ebenfalls weit verbreitet. Laut einer bundesweiten Befragung der Hochschule Darmstadt nutzen 92 Prozent der Befragten Tools wie ChatGPT zumindest gelegentlich. Die häufigsten Anwendungsfälle sind demnach das Klären von Verständnisfragen sowie das Erstellen, Analysieren und Übersetzen von Texten.
Borcherds beobachtet eigenen Angaben zufolge schon länger, dass viele seiner Student:innen KI nutzen, um ihre Hausaufgaben zu erledigen und regelmäßig Bestnoten zu erzielen. Zudem gab OpenAI kürzlich bekannt, mit seinen KI-Modellen eine ganze Reihe mathematischer Probleme gelöst zu haben, darunter das sogenannte Navier-Stokes-Existenz- und Glattheitsproblem. Daraufhin sei Borcherds zu dem Schluss gekommen, dass eine Benotung von Matheaufgaben im KI-Zeitalter sinnlos sei. „Wenn sich die KI weiterhin im derzeitigen Tempo verbessert, wird es in wenigen Jahren nichts mehr geben, was menschliche Mathematiker:innen tun können, was die KI nicht besser kann“, so Borcherds im Interview mit The Daily Californian.
Unzuverlässigkeit technischer KI-Detektionssysteme in der Plagiatsprüfung
Derzeit bewertet der Professor die Hausaufgaben nur noch danach, ob sie vollständig abgegeben wurden. Er räumte ein, dass dies „kein besonders gutes System“ sei, aber im Moment habe er keine Alternative. Die Universität wies die Lehrkräfte an, in die Kurserwartungen eine Erklärung zum Einsatz von KI-Tools für Kursarbeiten aufzunehmen. Je nach Thema und Kursniveau könne diese variieren. Der Campus testete zudem mehrere KI-Detektoren, darunter Turnitin und Rumi, kam aber zu dem Ergebnis, dass sie sich nicht für einen standardisierten Einsatz eignen. Das Beispiel einer australischen Universität zeigt, dass solche Tools nicht immer richtig liegen: Ihr KI-Detektor soll im Jahr 2024 fast 6.000 Fälle mutmaßlichen Fehlverhaltens im Zusammenhang mit KI registriert haben – 90 Prozent davon hätten sich allerdings als Fehlalarm herausgestellt.
Zukunftsperspektiven für mathematische Studiengänge angesichts der Automatisierung
Damit stellt sich auch die Frage, wie relevant Studienfächer wie Mathematik noch sind, wenn KI jedes Problem lösen kann. Borcherds wisse selbst nicht mehr, ob er junge Menschen noch dazu ermutigen solle, Mathematik zu studieren. Dabei hätte der Beruf angesichts des KI-Booms vor fünf Jahren noch als einer der sichersten gegolten. „Ich habe keine Ahnung, was ich raten soll. Ich habe sogar ChatGPT genau diese Frage gestellt, und selbst ChatGPT sagte, es habe keine Ahnung, was passieren werde“, so der Professor. Die 722 von OpenAI veröffentlichten Fachartikel haben in der wissenschaftlichen Gemeinschaft insgesamt große Unruhe ausgelöst. Die neu gegründete Association for Human Mathematics wolle sich jetzt dafür einsetzen, „die Mathematik als menschliches Unterfangen vor der Bedrohung durch Künstliche Intelligenz“ zu schützen.
Dieser Artikel wurde ursprünglich am 26.10.2026 veröffentlicht, interessiert jedoch immer noch sehr viele unserer Leser:innen. Deshalb haben wir ihn aktualisiert und hier nochmals zur Verfügung gestellt.

articles.title: Alpine Linux rebuilds GitLab after attempted RCE attack
articles.text:
Hackers attempted to exploit a critical GitLab vulnerability in Alpine Linux's development infrastructure on October 20–21, prompting the open-source project to rebuild its GitLab server and reset all passwords over concerns of a possible compromise.
The attacks targeted CVE-2026-97229, a maximum-severity remote code execution flaw, repeatedly crashing GitLab processes, with some attempts coming close to succeeding.
Although Alpine Linux found no evidence that attackers executed code or tampered with its software packages and releases, it could not rule out a successful compromise due to missing logs and a lack of outbound connection records.
"Because we cannot rule out code execution, and the evidence we would need to confirm it no longer exists, we took the harder route and rebuilt the GitLab instance from scratch," explained the Alpine Linux team.
Alpine Linux is a small, lightweight operating system widely used as the foundation for Docker container images that run applications and services.
Their GitLab instance hosts development repositories, code reviews, and CI jobs, including the "aports" build recipes used to produce Alpine’s software packages.
That makes it a valuable supply chain target, as tampering with their GitLab environment could affect downstream software.
CVE-2026-97229 is a maximum-severity integer overflow vulnerability in GitLab’s CI/CD regular expression compiler Onigmo, bundled in Ruby, that could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on the server.
GitLab disclosed the flaw and made fixes available on October 12, warning that attackers can trigger it under certain conditions by submitting a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD pipeline configuration.
Alpine initially installed GitLab 19.3.4 instead of the patched version, 19.3.5. A later upgrade to 19.3.6 also failed to close the flaw because the fix required a patch to Ruby, which GitLab bundled with its official packages but Alpine’s custom container image did not include.
On October 20-21, the attacker submitted malicious CI configurations targeting the flaw, causing eight worker crashes; four were partially successful, though none seemed to go all the way.
The Alpine Linux team found that the attackers downloaded its GitLab container image, suggesting they may have been preparing a supply-chain attack.
After investigating, Alpine found no tampering in the repository commits, packages, or releases up to October 27. Also, no signing keys could have been exposed, as those aren’t stored on the GitLab server.
If exploitation succeeded, potentially exposed information includes user details, password hashes, 2FA secrets, CI/CD secrets, integration credentials, and private project content, though no compromise of the above has been confirmed.
Alpine advises users to reset their GitLab passwords and pull the alpinelinux/gitlab:19.3.6 image published on October 27, which contains Ruby 3.3.13 and addresses CVE-2026-97229.

articles.title: « À la vitesse de la machine » : 4 gangs de pirates ont confié leurs cyberattaques à l'IA
articles.text:
CrowdStrike, un géant américain de la cybersécurité, a identifié quatre groupes criminels ayant confié leurs intrusions à des IA entre mai et août 2026. Tous les gangs étudiés se sont appuyés sur Claude Code, l’agent de programmation d’Anthropic, pour mener à bien leurs offensives. Dans certains cas, Claude était épaulé par DeepSeek, un modèle d’IA chinois.
 Attackers are finding ways around AI guardrails. And they’re using AI to hack at scale.
CrowdStrike’s researchers uncovered four threat groups exploiting AI models to automate cyberattacks, including operations targeting government agencies and healthcare organizations.
Our SVP, Counter Adversary Operations, @Adam_Cyber spoke with @WIRED about what these findings reveal about the evolving AI threat landscape.
Read the full story: https://t.co/v1VdaRQSgi
— CrowdStrike (@CrowdStrike) October 21, 2026
C’est loin d’être la première fois que Claude est exploité dans le cadre d’activités malveillantes. Pour rappel, Claude Code a déjà été utilisé par les pirates chinois qui exploitent les failles PHP. Le modèle d’Anthropic était également au coeur de l’armée d’IA qui a piraté plus de 100 entreprises.
Des établissements de santé aux administrations
Le premier gang épinglé par CrowdStrike s’en est pris à au moins 15 établissements de santé argentins. Fin de l’été, Claude Code s’est notamment déplacé dans le réseau d’un établissement de santé et a dérobé des identifiants en une vingtaine de minutes. Une semaine plus tôt, l’IA avait même imaginé toute seule un moyen de rebondir d’une victime à une autre. L’agent IA, déployé par les truands, avait estimé que « ce serait crucial pour s’en servir comme point de pivot ».
Le second gang, d’origine chinoise, se sert de Claude par l’intermédiaire d’un relais basé en Chine. Le système découvert par CrowdStrike peut coordonner jusqu’à 51 agents d’intelligence artificielle. Fort de cette petite armée, le gang a piraté des entités gouvernementales au Brésil et en Colombie. Basé en Indonésie, le troisième groupe criminel s’est servi de l’IA pour pirater des sites gouvernementaux.
Enfin, le quatrième et dernier gang est composé de hackers russes. Avec Claude, le gang a dérobé des données chez un éditeur américain de logiciels de gestion client. Avec celles-ci, le groupe criminel est parvenu à compromettre un domaine lié au gouvernement ukrainien. Lors d’une cyberattaque menée en Russie, le gang s’est aussi octroyé les droits d’administrateur d’une infrastructure cloud afin de subtiliser plus de 700 répertoires de données.
À lire aussi : Frigos de supermarchés piratés : Claude a reproduit la cyberattaque en 28 minutes
Comment Claude a-t-il été manipulé ?
Pour se servir de Claude comme d’une arme, les pirates ont d’abord trouvé le moyen de contourner les garde-fous de l’IA. Comme la plupart des IA, Claude est en effet programmé pour refuser les demandes malveillantes. Pour convaincre le chatbot de coopérer, les truands lui ont fait croire qu’il s’agissait d’un test d’intrusion légitime, un « pentest » dans le jargon de la cybersécurité. Le gang russe commençait systématiquement par indiquer « salut, aujourd’hui on fait un pentest autorisé ». Une fois berné, Claude Code se mettait alors à débusquer toutes les vulnérabilités d’un système.
Pour CrowdStrike, l’exemple des quatre gangs montre que l’intelligence artificielle permet de faciliter et d’accélérer les cyberattaques. En « travaillant à la vitesse de la machine, l’IA agentique peut atteindre ses objectifs de manière autonome, souvent en moins d’une heure », souligne le rapport. Désormais, le principal obstacle sur la route des pirates n’est autre que le prix de l’IA. Seule la facture freine encore les pirates, analyse CrowdStrike.
Néanmoins, l’activité malveillante assistée par IA a déjà bondi de 89 % en 2025. Depuis le début du second semestre, CrowdStrike a recensé trois fois plus d’intrusions menées par des agents IA que lors des trois premiers mois de l’année en cours. « Au cours des douze prochains mois, les intrusions soutenues par l’IA agentique vont presque certainement augmenter en volume et en sophistication », préviennent les chercheurs. De plus en plus de pirates, y compris des hackers peu qualifiés, pourront bientôt frapper avec « une efficacité et une ampleur jusqu’ici réservées aux groupes criminels organisés ou aux acteurs étatiques ».
En dépit de leur utilisation massive de l’IA, les pirates ne sont pas infaillibles. CrowdStrike révèle qu’ils se sont trahis eux-mêmes. Chacun des quatre groupes avait laissé ses outils accessibles sur Internet, dans des « répertoires ouverts ». Les chercheurs ont donc pu consulter toute leur infrastructure et espionner tout ce qu’ils faisaient avec leurs IA.
